people.bio: Chaitanya Desai has two bachelor's degrees from the University of Pennsylvania: chemical engineering and economics (Wharton). He joined Apar in 1993 in the polymer division, which had a technical tie-up with Goodyear. He turned that business around and ran it for 15 years until it was sold to a European multinational. He then took charge of the conductor business and also has a strategic role in cables. He sits on IEEMA's executive council. He was up for re-appointment by rotation at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Rishabh K. Desai
people.since: Whole-time director from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2030 (earlier a non-executive director)
people.relation: Son of Kushal Desai; nephew of Chaitanya Desai
people.bio: Rishabh Desai has a bachelor's in business management and entrepreneurship from Babson College in the US (2014). He worked for a year at Ergon, a US oil refiner, then led the construction of a factory in 2015 and operations in the Middle East and North Africa. He now runs the speciality oils business and is the only executive director paid partly by a subsidiary. He moved from non-executive to whole-time director in September 2025.

people.name: Ramesh S. Iyer
people.bio: Ramesh Iyer is a chartered accountant, cost accountant and company secretary. He had about 22 years in finance when he joined Apar as CFO on 3 February 2022. Before that he was CFO of Nitco from 2020 to 2021.

people.name: Chandrashekhar Shrotri
people.bio: Chandrashekhar Shrotri has more than 35 years in sales, marketing, business development, product management and general management across India, Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East. Before Apar he was at Siemens, most recently as Segment CEO for a region covering South Asia, Southeast Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and Australia (22 countries). He replaced Shashi Amin, who resigned in December 2025.

people.name: Manish Agrawal
people.role: CEO, Conductors & Telecommunications; MD, APAR T&D
people.since: Listed on the company's management page
people.bio: Manish Agrawal runs the conductor and telecom cable businesses and is managing director of APAR T&D. He has more than 27 years in the power and telecom sectors and specialises in transmission and distribution. The company describes him as a Harvard alumnus but does not name the programme.

companies.changes: Cables CEO Shashi Amin resigned in December 2025; Chandrashekhar Shrotri replaced him from 4 December 2025. Rishabh Desai became a whole-time director on 1 September 2025. A ₹2,500cr QIP in August 2026 diluted the promoters.

companies.styleNote: Genus is part of the Kailash Group of the Agarwal family. Ishwar Chand Agarwal is Executive Chairman. Two of his sons are executives: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal (MD & CEO) and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal (Joint MD). A third son, Kailash Chandra Agarwal, is non-executive Vice-Chairman. Each of the three executives was paid about ₹21cr in FY26. Promoters own about 39%, mostly through group companies.

people.name: Ishwar Chand Agarwal
people.since: Board since 1994; current term 24 January 2024 to 23 January 2029
people.relation: Promoter; father of Kailash Chandra, Rajendra Kumar and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.stake: 0.89% in his own name (27,02,491 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 39%
people.bio: Ishwar Chand Agarwal is a commerce graduate with more than five decades in business. The family group spans power infrastructure, paper, coal and coke, apparel and agricultural commodities. He is described as focused on strategy, expansion and succession planning. He is 76, has been on the board since May 1994, and was paid ₹21.2cr in FY26. He is also a director of other group companies, including Kailash Industries and Genus Paper & Boards.

people.name: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal
people.since: Board since 2001; current term 29 May 2024 to 28 May 2029
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Ishwar Chand Agarwal; brother of Kailash Chandra and Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.bio: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal has a B.E. in electronics. He has spent his career in power distribution, covering smart metering, smart grid, solar panels and batteries. He sets the company's strategy and product direction and oversees technology, R&D, alliances and partnerships. He joined the board in January 2001, is 50, and was paid ₹20.6cr in FY26.

people.name: Jitendra Kumar Agarwal
people.since: Board since 2004; current term 20 September 2024 to 19 September 2029
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Ishwar Chand Agarwal; brother of Kailash Chandra and Rajendra Kumar Agarwal
people.bio: Jitendra Kumar Agarwal has an MBA in marketing. He leads marketing, branding and sales in power distribution and power backup, including finding new business, trade shows and digital marketing. He also has experience with operating-expenditure (Opex) business models such as the smart-meter contracts. He joined the board in May 2004, is 49, and was paid ₹20.6cr in FY26.

people.name: Nathu Lal Nama
people.since: Whole-time director from 9 February 2026 (2-year term); CFO until 18 May 2026
people.bio: Nathu Lal Nama is a chartered accountant with more than 36 years in finance and accounts, covering planning, budgeting, audits, working capital, costing and internal controls. He was Genus's chief finance officer and joined the board as a whole-time director in February 2026. When a new CFO was hired in May 2026 he gave up the CFO role but stayed on the board as an executive director. He is 61.

people.name: Vinod Raheja
people.bio: Vinod Raheja is a chartered accountant with more than 33 years in senior finance roles, including as CFO in several industries. His experience covers M&A, restructuring, fundraising, working capital, taxation, risk management and ERP/SAP systems. The company did not name his earlier employers. He is 57 and joined as CFO on 18 May 2026.

companies.changes: Vinod Raheja became CFO on 18 May 2026, and Nathu Lal Nama moved out of the CFO role but stayed as a whole-time director. Two chief human resources officers left in FY26 (June 2025 and March 2026); a third joined in May 2026.

companies.styleNote: A founder-family company. Founder R. Doraiswamy, 83, is Managing Director and his elder son D. Rajesh Kumar is Joint MD. His younger son Vishnu Rangaswamy is a non-executive director. A CFO was hired from outside in April 2026; before that the Joint MD also acted as CFO. Promoters own 37.5%, much of it through group companies.

people.name: R. Doraiswamy
people.relation: Founder; father of D. Rajesh Kumar (Joint MD) and Vishnu Rangaswamy (director)
people.bio: R. Doraiswamy is an electrical engineering graduate who has run Salzer since it started in 1985. The company credits him with bringing the Salzer group's electrical installation products up to international quality standards. Shareholders re-appointed him for three years from 1 May 2026 by postal ballot, at 83. The terms are a monthly salary of ₹6.5 lakh plus 2.5% of net profit as commission. He was paid about ₹1.1cr in FY25.

people.name: D. Rajesh Kumar
people.since: More than three decades at Salzer; Joint MD (and CFO until 31 March 2026); re-appointment for 5 years from 1 October 2026 put to the September 2026 AGM
people.relation: Son of the founder-MD, R. Doraiswamy; elder brother of director Vishnu Rangaswamy
people.bio: Rajesh Kumar has worked at Salzer for more than 30 years in finance, planning, treasury and operations. He was Joint MD and CFO (latest term from October 2021) until April 2026, when a separate CFO was hired, and he stayed on as Joint MD. The board credits him with capacity expansion, product diversification and about 23% sales growth a year over the last five years. He is also a director of group companies including Kaycee Industries (a listed subsidiary), Salzer Exports and Salzer EV Infra, and a nominee director on Ultrafast Chargers, its EV-charger partner.

people.name: Raman Krishnamoorthy (K. Raman)
people.bio: K. Raman joined as CFO on 1 April 2026, taking the CFO role from Joint MD Rajesh Kumar. Management said he was hired to strengthen financial governance and planning for the next phase of growth. The company has not published his education or earlier employers.

people.name: M. Lakshminarayana
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: M. Lakshminarayana heads operations and is first on the list of senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his background.

companies.changes: K. Raman became CFO on 1 April 2026; Rajesh Kumar gave up the CFO title and stayed Joint MD. In FY26 some designated insiders made contra trades and traded during the closed window. They paid back ₹4.8 lakh of profit and ₹3.25 lakh of penalties, and the company reported this to SEBI in March 2026.

companies.styleNote: A single family runs it. Founder Ashok Kumar Agarwal is Chairman & MD, his son Ankit Agrawal is CEO, and Ankit's wife Neha Agarwal is a whole-time director and also acting CFO. There has been no dedicated CFO since April 2025. The three executives have personally guaranteed bank loans and lent money to the company. Promoters own about 52%.

people.name: Ashok Kumar Agarwal
people.relation: Founder; father of Ankit Agrawal; father-in-law of Neha Agarwal
people.stake: 22.64% (FY26 annual report); promoter family together about 52%
people.bio: Ashok Kumar Agarwal founded the company in 1994 in a small workshop in Jaipur's Malviya Nagar. It began as a metal-castings business and grew into switchgear panels, meter boxes and enclosures for power utilities. He has more than four decades in the electrical industry. He sets strategy and chairs the board, and the company says his recent focus has been certified 'intelligent' products such as PulseBox and how capital is spent. The company has not published his education.

people.name: Ankit Agrawal
people.relation: Son of the founder, Ashok Kumar Agarwal; husband of Neha Agarwal
people.bio: Ankit Agrawal has 23 years in the industry. He runs growth, diversification and the technology programme, and is responsible for sales, marketing and quality. He is the company's main contact for investors and analysts. The company's Jaipur premises include plots he owns personally. He raised his stake from 9.7% to 17.7% during FY26. The company has not published his education.

people.name: Neha Agarwal
people.role: Whole-time Director & Chief Financial Officer (additional charge)
people.since: Board since June 2016; acting CFO since 4 July 2025
people.relation: Wife of CEO Ankit Agrawal; daughter-in-law of the Chairman & MD
people.bio: Neha Agarwal has about 14–16 years in management, administration and operations at the company, and oversees daily operations. She took the extra charge of CFO on 4 July 2025 after CFO Anand Chaturvedi left in April 2025. She is steering the move to Main Board reporting. She also leads the company's CSR work and is a director of the solar subsidiaries RMC Green Energy and RMC Solar One, Two, Three and Five. She was born in 1982.

people.name: Manish Mantri
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Manish Mantri is a chemical engineering graduate of MREC (now MNIT) Jaipur with about 30 years in manufacturing and services. He set up new plants at the Aditya Birla Group and RR Kabel, led high-voltage and extra-high-voltage projects at Sterlite Technologies, and managed large EPC and EHV projects at KEI Industries.

people.name: Vikash Verma
people.bio: Vikash Verma has been a chartered accountant since 2005 and has more than 22 years of experience. He previously worked at South Asia LPG Company, the joint venture between Hindustan Petroleum and TotalEnergies. He is one of two chartered accountants hired in the second quarter of FY26 to rebuild the finance team, and was later named senior management.

people.name: Sajal Kumar Ghosh
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Sajal Kumar Ghosh has 33 years in Indian manufacturing and specialises in polymers and composites. His work covers materials science, product development, technical services and R&D. It supports the SMC and FRP moulding capability that the PulseBox smart box relies on.

companies.changes: CFO Anand Chaturvedi left on 16 April 2025, and Neha Agarwal has held the CFO role as an additional charge since July 2025. Shivani Bairathi became company secretary in June 2025. The company moved to BSE's Main Board and listed on NSE on 1 April 2026.

companies.styleNote: Part of the INOXGFL group controlled by Vivek Jain's family. His son Devansh Jain, who started the company, is a whole-time director and leads the group's renewables businesses. A hired CEO runs day-to-day operations, and the group's renewables CEO sits above him. Promoters own about 44%, mainly through Inox Leasing & Finance (27.7%) and two LLPs. The 2026 AGM notice seeks approval for loans of up to ₹600cr from Devansh Jain.

people.name: Devansh Jain
people.since: Started Inox Wind in 2009; whole-time director
people.relation: Promoter; son of INOXGFL group chairman Vivek Jain
people.stake: 0.004% in his own name (63,200 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 44%
people.bio: Devansh Jain has a double major in economics and business administration from Carnegie Mellon University in the US. He set up Inox Wind as the group's move into renewables, took it public in 2015 and listed Inox Green, a wind-farm maintenance company, in 2022. He is also building INOX Solar (solar cells and modules), GFCL EV (battery chemicals) and INOX Clean Energy, an IPP with about 3,000 MW of wind and solar capacity. He has held roles at PHDCCI, FICCI, IWPA and YPO, and was on Fortune's '40 Under 40' list in 2023–2025.

people.name: Manoj Dixit
people.since: Re-appointed for 2 years from 3 December 2025; with the INOXGFL group since 2008
people.bio: Manoj Dixit has a master's in mechanical engineering and more than 27 years in power project development, power scheduling, land acquisition and regulatory approvals. Before joining the INOXGFL group in 2008 he worked at Perfect Refractories and Gujarat Fluorochemicals.

people.name: Sanjeev Agarwal
people.bio: Sanjeev Agarwal has a mechanical engineering degree from IIT Roorkee and an MBA from Pune University. He has more than 34 years in project execution, sales, supply chain and change management across T&D, fossil power and nuclear steam turbines, in Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Europe. He previously worked at TBW, Alstom, GE and KEC International. He became CEO on 1 June 2025, replacing Kailash Lal Tarachandani, who moved up to group CEO for renewables.

people.name: Kailash Lal Tarachandani
people.role: Group Chief Executive Officer, Renewables Business
people.since: Joined as CEO in May 2013; group renewables CEO from June 2025
people.bio: Kailash Tarachandani has a B.Tech in electrical engineering from IIT Kanpur and an MBA from INSEAD. He has more than 30 years in strategy, global project execution, product management and business development, including setting up plants and acquiring technologies. Before joining Inox Wind as CEO in May 2013 he worked at Kenersys (Pune), Vestas Wind Systems, Alstom Power in Switzerland and Larsen & Toubro. In June 2025 he became group CEO of the renewables business.

people.name: Shivam Tandon
people.since: CFO (earlier CFO of Inox Wind Energy)
people.bio: Shivam Tandon is a chartered accountant with more than 17 years in manufacturing finance: reporting, budgeting, cost control, banking, tax and audit. Before the INOXGFL group he worked at the BC Jindal Group, Samvardhana Motherson and Tata Steel. His previous role was CFO of Inox Wind Energy.

companies.changes: Sanjeev Agarwal replaced Kailash Tarachandani as CEO on 1 June 2025. Non-executive director Urvashi Saxena left on 30 June 2025. Manoj Dixit was re-appointed as whole-time director from December 2025.

companies.styleNote: The Nahata family controls it. Anant Nahata, son of HFCL founder Mahendra Nahata, is MD & CEO. The promoter stake of about 66% is held through NextWave Communications (54.7%), Satellite Finance and HFCL; Anant holds no shares personally. The non-executive chairman, Himanshu Baid, is MD of Poly Medicure. Hired CEOs run the EV-charger and critical-power businesses.

people.name: Anant Nahata
people.since: Board since June 2008; employed since July 2017
people.relation: Promoter; son of Mahendra Nahata, founder and MD of HFCL (a promoter shareholder)
people.stake: nil personally (FY26 annual report); promoter group about 66%, mainly through NextWave Communications
people.bio: Anant Nahata has a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Pennsylvania. He worked in investment banking at Credit Suisse in New York and later founded the online fashion retailer Koovs. In the late 2000s he promoted Infotel Broadband, which won all-India spectrum and was sold to Reliance. He has been on Exicom's board since 2008 and full-time since 2017. Under him the company expanded from telecom power systems into EV chargers, listed in March 2024 and bought the Australian fast-charger maker Tritium. He is 42 and was paid ₹2.1cr in FY26.

people.name: Vivekanand Kumar
people.since: With Exicom since 2021; re-appointed at the 2025 AGM
people.bio: Vivekanand Kumar is an engineer with a postgraduate business degree and more than 20 years in manufacturing, operations and supply chain. Before Exicom he held leadership roles at Autoliv India, Gates India, GKN Driveline India, Caparo Engineering India and Roop Automotives. The company credits him with strengthening its manufacturing and operations.

people.name: Shiraz Khanna
people.bio: Shiraz Khanna is a chartered accountant with more than 30 years of experience. He has been CFO since 2021 and also oversees accounts, treasury, tax, compliance and legal. Before Exicom he held senior finance roles at PwC India, Aircel, Bharti Airtel and American Express.

people.name: Anshuman Divyanshu
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Anshuman Divyanshu has nearly 20 years in energy, mobility and infrastructure. He held leadership roles at BPCL, Reliance Industries and Reliance BP Mobility, where he helped build Jio-bp's EV charging network into one of India's largest charge-point operators. He runs Exicom's EV-charger division.

people.name: Sanjeev Kumar Narula
people.bio: Sanjeev Narula has a B.Tech and runs the critical power business, which grew out of Exicom's original telecom power business. Before Exicom he held leadership roles at Mahindra & Mahindra, Honda Siel Power Products and TAFE, and grew businesses in India, the SAARC region, Africa and the Middle East. He joined in September 2022.

people.name: Puran Mal Singh
people.bio: Puran Mal Singh has led Exicom's research and development since joining in 2011, with a focus on power electronics and product development. He previously worked at Delta Power Solutions.

companies.changes: No KMP or senior management changes in FY26. Vice President (Manufacturing) Aman Sharma resigned with effect from 30 June 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Raman Bhatia is Managing Director and his wife Sarika Bhatia is a whole-time director. Other Bhatia relatives are in the promoter group, including former CFO Vikas Bhatia, who now heads field execution. Promoters own about 59%. The board elects a chairman at each meeting rather than having a standing one.

people.name: Raman Bhatia
people.relation: Founder and promoter; husband of Sarika Bhatia
people.stake: 29.91% (FY26 annual report); his HUF holds another 13.40%; promoter family together about 59%
people.bio: Raman Bhatia founded Servotech and has run it as MD since it began. He started in business in 1991, first with a TV repair business, before moving into power products. He took the company from traditional power backup products into solar, EV chargers, power electronics and batteries, and listed it on NSE. The company has not published his education. The 2026 AGM notice proposed pay of up to ₹1.8cr a year for him.

people.name: Sarika Bhatia
people.since: Whole-time director; re-appointment proposed at the 2026 AGM
people.relation: Wife of the founder-MD, Raman Bhatia
people.bio: Sarika Bhatia runs sales and marketing and has more than 17 years in leadership roles at the company. The company says she handles client relationships and winning large tenders and projects. The company has not published her education.

people.name: Mrityunjay Kumar Jha
people.since: 24 July 2026 (3-year term, subject to shareholder approval)
people.bio: Mrityunjay Kumar Jha has worked at Servotech for 17 years in human resources, administration, employee relations and organisational development. He joined the board as a whole-time director on 24 July 2026, the day after Executive Director (HR) Digvijay Kapoor left. His proposed pay is up to ₹24 lakh a year.

people.name: Vipin Kaushik
people.bio: Vipin Kaushik is a chartered accountant with a postgraduate degree from Gujarat University, and holds diplomas in international financial reporting (ACCA) and management and business finance (ICAI). He has more than 20 years in corporate finance, strategy, accounts, tax and compliance. He has worked in senior roles, including as CFO, at ICICI Bank, Delhivery, V2 Retail and Franchise India Group. He was already at Servotech and was promoted to CFO on 1 April 2026, replacing Vikas Bhatia.

people.name: Arun Handa
people.since: Listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Arun Handa is Servotech's Chief Technical Officer and is named as senior management in the FY26 annual report. The company has not published his background.

companies.changes: CFO Vikas Bhatia (promoter group) stepped down on 31 March 2026 and is now Head of Field Execution; Vipin Kaushik became CFO on 1 April 2026. Executive Director (HR) Digvijay Kapoor, appointed in June 2025, left on 23 July 2026, and Mrityunjay Kumar Jha joined the board as a whole-time director on 24 July 2026. NSE fined the company twice in FY26 (August and November 2025) for late compliance with Regulation 17(1A), the rule on non-executive directors over 75.

companies.styleNote: The Mehta family controls it. Bhavna Mehta owns 56.3% and the promoter group 58.6%. In February 2026 she stepped down as MD but stayed on the board as a non-executive director. Her husband Dr. Harshad Mehta is non-executive Chairman and their daughter Sonali Mehta is a non-executive director. A hired MD & CEO, N. Ramesh Kumar, now runs the company. The ₹42cr silicon-carbide know-how was bought from Sicamore Semiconductor (US), which the accounts list as an entity in which a director or relative is interested.

people.name: N. Ramesh Kumar (Ramesh Kumar Narasinghbhan)
people.bio: Ramesh Kumar has a B.E. in electrical engineering from MNNIT Allahabad and more than 42 years in electrical equipment. He started in 1984 as a graduate engineer trainee at GEC of India and joined Crompton Greaves in 1990, where he spent nearly three decades. There he ran motors, pumps, lighting, fans, appliances, transformers and switchgear, and rose to President of CG's India businesses and then President of the industrial business at CG Power. Most recently he was CEO of Diffusion Engineers. He has attended leadership programmes at IIM Ahmedabad, ISB-Kellogg and Management Centre Europe, and was vice-president of IFMA and an elected member of ELCOMA. He is 63. His fixed pay is ₹1.9cr a year plus up to ₹40 lakh variable pay and a ₹30 lakh joining bonus.

people.name: Ramesh Gopal Trasi
people.since: CEO for more than 22 years until February 2026; CTO since then
people.bio: R. G. Trasi ran RIR as CEO for more than 22 years and also acted as CFO. When the new MD & CEO joined in February 2026 he moved to Chief Technology Officer, to lead its technology and innovation plan. He resigned as CFO on 2 June 2026, citing his other responsibilities.

companies.changes: Bhavna Mehta stepped down as MD and R. G. Trasi as CEO in February 2026; N. Ramesh Kumar became MD & CEO on 11 February 2026. Trasi also resigned as CFO on 2 June 2026, and we found no announcement of a replacement. Independent director Kaushal Mehta resigned in July 2025.

companies.styleNote: Part of the KP Group. Its founder, Dr. Faruk G. Patel, is non-executive Chairman and personally owns 57.9%. His son Hassan Patel is a whole-time director, and the long-serving engineer Muinulhaque Kadva runs the factories. The company pays the promoter a 2% brand royalty (₹19.2cr in FY26), and ₹32.9cr of 'advance for property' was outstanding to Faruk Patel in March 2026. A large part of its revenue comes from other KP Group companies.

people.name: Muinulhaque Kadva
people.since: With the company for over a decade; whole-time director
people.bio: Muinulhaque Iqbalhusen Kadva has a mechanical engineering degree from Gujarat Technological University and has been with the company for more than ten years. He heads manufacturing, running the factories and project execution. His expertise covers galvanising, fabrication, telecom towers and support structures for renewable projects. He is involved in day-to-day management and strategic decisions, and is one of the company's designated officials for disclosure.

people.name: Hassan Faruk Patel
people.relation: Promoter; son of the founder and Chairman, Dr. Faruk G. Patel
people.stake: 0.01% (6,117 shares, FY26 annual report); his father holds 57.87%
people.bio: Hassan Patel has a BBA from AURO University, Surat. He leads human resources for the KP Group and is also involved in overall management, finance, strategic planning and decisions at KP Green. He became a whole-time director in September 2025 and was paid ₹32.6 lakh in FY26. He is also a director of several group companies, including green hydrogen and ammonia, energy storage and O&M units. He retires by rotation and is up for re-appointment at the September 2026 AGM.

people.name: Pravinkumar Singh
people.bio: Pravinkumar Singh has a commerce degree from South Gujarat University. He has experience in financial management, planning, risk assessment, corporate finance and compliance, according to the company's website. The company has not published his earlier employers.

companies.changes: Hassan Patel became a whole-time director on 29 September 2025. On 3 July 2026 non-executive director Amit Khandelwal resigned, and Prof. Sunil Kumar Maheshwari (formerly of IIM Ahmedabad) joined as non-executive Vice-Chairman, subject to approval at the September 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: A Patel family business from Anand, Gujarat. Brothers Niral Patel (Chairman & MD) and Amish Patel run it with their first cousin Tanmay Patel as whole-time directors. The long-time director Krupeshbhai Patel died in August 2025. A hired CEO, Akshaykumar Mathur, runs day-to-day operations. Promoters and the family trust own about 87%.

people.name: Niral K. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Amish Patel and first cousin of Tanmay Patel
people.stake: 8.29% (63,75,000 shares, FY26 annual report); promoter group together about 87%
people.bio: Niral Patel, 44, has a computer engineering degree from the University of Pune, a diploma in electrical engineering from the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education and an MBA from Hult International Business School. He has more than 22 years in transformer making. At Atlanta he handles customer and supplier relationships, strategy and budgets. He is also linked to several family companies, including Amod Stampings, Auro Stampings, Venus Laminations and the Neptune realty firms. Amod Stampings is a large parts supplier to Atlanta, so related-party purchases are worth watching.

people.name: Tanmay S. Patel
people.since: With the company since 2002; director since July 2002
people.relation: Promoter; first cousin of Niral and Amish Patel
people.bio: Tanmay Patel, 48, has a diploma in electrical engineering from the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education. He has more than 22 years in the transformer, electrical and manufacturing industries, all of it at Atlanta, which he joined in 2002. He is responsible for buying raw materials and components and for supply-chain logistics.

people.name: Amish K. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Niral Patel and first cousin of Tanmay Patel
people.bio: Amish Patel, 42, has a bachelor's degree in business administration from Sardar Patel University. He has about 17 years of experience in real estate, investment and acquisitions, and is also associated with the family's Neptune Realty. He joined Atlanta's board in 2022. His job is to find suitable land for new plants and to work with project managers and contractors on building them.

people.name: Akshaykumar B. Mathur
people.bio: Akshaykumar Mathur has a B.Tech in electronics and communication from Kakatiya University and an MBA from the University of Jodhpur. He has about 44 years of work experience, 32 of them in the transformer industry, and previously worked at Voltamp Transformers. He joined Atlanta in August 2015 and signs the CEO certificate on the accounts. He is the senior hired manager in a family-led company.

people.name: Mehul S. Mehta
people.bio: Mehul Mehta has a commerce degree and a postgraduate diploma in business administration from Sardar Patel University, plus a diploma in business management, an advanced diploma in management and an MBA from ICFAI University, Dehradun. He previously worked at ABG Cement. He joined Atlanta in March 2005 and has about 19 years of experience in finance.

people.name: Anand Sharma
people.bio: Anand Sharma has an engineering diploma from Dayalbagh Educational Institute and a postgraduate diploma in business administration (operations) from the Symbiosis Centre for Distance Learning. Before joining Atlanta in March 2022 he worked at Crompton Greaves, EMCO, Caparo Fasteners, NLMK India Service Center, Hotline Glass and BTA Cellcom. He is listed as senior management.

people.name: Minesh Bhatt
people.bio: Minesh Bhatt has a diploma in electrical engineering from Government Polytechnic, Chhotaudaipur. He previously worked at Voltamp Transformers and joined Atlanta in April 2004. He has 23 years of engineering experience and heads transformer design, which matters as the company moves up to 400 kV and 765 kV units.

companies.changes: Whole-time director Krupeshbhai Patel died on 7 August 2025; his shares are being transferred. No executive changes filed since the annual report (27 August 2026).

companies.styleNote: Two managing directors share the top job. The promoter Kunjal Patel, who owns 30%, is Vice Chairman & MD. The Chairman & MD, Kanubhai Patel, is a chartered accountant who has worked for the group since 1982 and is not related to the promoter. Kunjal Patel's relative Taral Patel is a non-executive director. Promoter holding fell from 38% to 30% after a 7.8% block sale in September 2025.

people.name: Kanubhai S. Patel
people.since: Joined 1992 as CEO; executive director 1995; joint MD 2002; Chairman & MD since 2013
people.relation: Not related to the promoter or any director
people.bio: Kanubhai Patel, 69, is a commerce graduate, a fellow chartered accountant and a fellow company secretary, and attended an advanced management programme at Kellogg in the US. He worked for the group as a professional from 1982 and moved to Voltamp in 1992 as CEO. He became executive director in 1995, joint managing director in 2002 and chairman & managing director in 2013. The company credits him with shifting it from utility tenders to private industrial customers, keeping it debt-free since 2005-06 and taking it public in 2006. He is also an independent director of Epigral and Paramount.

people.name: Kunjal L. Patel
people.relation: Promoter; related to non-executive director Taral K. Patel
people.stake: 30.00% (30,35,176 shares, FY26 annual report); down from 37.80% a year earlier
people.bio: Kunjal Patel has an electrical engineering degree from M. S. University of Vadodara and attended INSEAD. He joined Voltamp in 1994 and has worked across production, marketing, after-sales service and general management. He now oversees purchasing and planning, quality control, manufacturing, transformer design and the service business. He is the company's only promoter shareholder of size, and sold 7.8% of the company in a block deal in September 2025.

people.name: Vijay Gupta
people.since: COO from November 2025; with the company about 18 years
people.bio: Vijay Gupta has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering and an MBA. He has about 33 years in the transformer industry, including 15 years in the transformer business of Crompton Greaves. He joined Voltamp about 18 years ago and ran its power-transformer business unit before being promoted to COO in November 2025.

people.name: Shailesh Prajapati
people.bio: Shailesh Prajapati is a chartered accountant. He joined Voltamp in 2018 and was General Manager – Accounts & Finance before becoming CFO in May 2022, when the long-serving CFO Vallabh Madhani retired. At his appointment he had about 14 years of experience in accounts, banking and finance, direct and indirect tax and statutory compliance.

companies.changes: Vijay Gupta promoted to COO on 8 November 2025. No executive changes filed since the annual report (7 July 2026).

companies.styleNote: Founded in 1981 by Jitendra Mamtora, who is Chairman and a whole-time director. His son Satyen Mamtora is MD & CEO, and his wife Karuna Mamtora is an executive director. A hired CEO lasted only six months (July 2025 to January 2026), after which Satyen took the CEO title too. Promoters own about 64%; lenders hold a pledge over about 14% of the company's shares owned by a director.

people.name: Jitendra U. Mamtora
people.since: Founder (1981); Chairman since incorporation in 1994; re-appointed from 1 January 2026
people.relation: Founder; husband of Karuna Mamtora and father of Satyen Mamtora
people.stake: 31.30% (9,39,63,368 shares, FY26 annual report); family together about 50%, promoter group about 64%
people.bio: Jitendra Mamtora has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College. He started in 1969 as an engineer at Electrical Equipment Manufacturing Company and set up Transformers and Rectifiers in Gujarat in 1981, first making distribution transformers and then furnace transformers. He has more than 40 years in the industry and has built the company into a maker of units up to 1,200 kV. He sits on the executive council of IEEMA, the electrical equipment makers' association, has chaired its transformer division since 2007, and is active in CII and FICCI.

people.name: Satyen J. Mamtora
people.since: Director since July 1994; CEO title added 8 January 2026
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, Jitendra Mamtora, and of Karuna Mamtora
people.bio: Satyen Mamtora, born in 1974, has a diploma in electrical engineering from Uxbridge College in London. He has been with the company since its early years and was trained in rotation across all key functions. He runs production and marketing, built the company's position with state and central power utilities, and set up its global marketing plan. Under him sales crossed ₹2,000cr in FY25. He took over the CEO role in January 2026 after the hired CEO, Mukul Srivastava, resigned.

people.name: Karuna J. Mamtora
people.since: Executive director since April 2005; re-appointed from 1 April 2026
people.relation: Wife of the Chairman, Jitendra Mamtora; mother of Satyen Mamtora
people.bio: Karuna Mamtora has a bachelor's degree in arts from Gujarat University. She has been involved with the company since its early days and became an executive director in April 2005. She handles general administration and human resources and leads the company's CSR programmes as chairperson of the CSR committee.

people.name: Mehul Shah
people.bio: Mehul Shah is a chartered accountant with more than 26 years of experience in accounting, financial operations, fund management, budgeting, tax and corporate governance. Before joining TARIL he worked at Nirma, Adani Enterprises, Reliance Logistics, Arvind SmartSpaces, Gujarat Ambuja Exports and Asian Granito India. He replaced Chanchal Rajora as CFO in March 2026, as the company spends heavily on backward integration.

people.name: Chanchal S. S. Rajora
people.since: Director Finance from November 2025; CFO until 5 March 2026
people.bio: Dr. Chanchal Rajora is a chartered accountant with about 25 years of experience in corporate finance, fund raising, financial planning, mergers and acquisitions, and credit and risk management. He was the company's CFO and adviser to the board, and was made Director – Finance in November 2025. He stepped down as CFO in March 2026 in what the company called a strategic restructuring, and stays on as senior management.

companies.changes: Hired CEO Mukul Srivastava (joined July 2025) resigned on 7 January 2026 for personal reasons; Satyen Mamtora became MD & CEO. CFO Chanchal Rajora handed over to Mehul Shah on 5 March 2026 and stays as Director – Finance. The company website now lists Bhavin Vahia as HR head in place of Ajay Bamzai named in the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Run by its two co-founders, who are not related to each other: Vee Rajmohan (Chairman & MD) and K. V. Pradeep Kumar (whole-time director). Both were re-appointed for three years from 31 August 2026. Both are also partners in Danya Electric Company, a transformer firm in which Supreme holds a 90% profit share, trades with it and guarantees its loans. The two founders own 52% between them; the promoter group about 57%.

people.name: Vee Rajmohan
people.since: Founder (partnership firm 2001); director since June 2005; re-appointed to August 2029
people.relation: Co-founder; not related to any director
people.stake: 31.51% (78,75,430 shares, FY26 annual report); founders together 52%
people.bio: Vee Rajmohan, 55, started in 1990 as works manager at Venuss Herbo Aromatics in Rajapalayam, Tamil Nadu, where he set up and commissioned the plant; he stayed until 2001. That year he and Pradeep Kumar founded the partnership Supreme Power Equipments to make distribution transformers for the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board, and in 2005 turned it into a private company. The FY26 annual report lists a bachelor's degree in engineering, while the 2023 IPO prospectus said he had enrolled for one; he also holds an honorary doctorate in business. He leads strategy, business development and expansion, including the new 220 kV Kannur plant. He holds a 7.5% profit share in Danya Electric Company, a related party.

people.name: K. V. Pradeep Kumar (Vishwambran Nair Pradeep Kumar)
people.since: Co-founder (2001); whole-time director since June 2023; re-appointed to August 2029
people.relation: Co-founder; not related to any director
people.bio: Pradeep Kumar, 55, has a bachelor's degree in engineering. He joined Indotech Transformers (now Prolec GE) in Chennai as a quality-assurance trainee engineer in 1991 and by 1997 headed quality assurance for transformers up to 100 MVA and 230 kV. He co-founded Supreme with Vee Rajmohan and is its technical lead, overseeing manufacturing, quality, procurement and design. He developed the company's wind-turbine and inverter-duty transformer designs, sold to many wind and solar plants. He holds a 2.5% profit share in Danya Electric Company.

people.name: Thulasiraman Boologa Nathan
people.bio: Thulasiraman Boologa Nathan has a B.Com and has passed the intermediate level of the cost accountancy (ICWA) course. He has more than 30 years of experience in finance, accounts, costing and budgeting. Before joining Supreme he was senior manager, finance and accounts, at Vetrivel Forgings. He became CFO in September 2023, just before the company's December 2023 SME IPO.

companies.changes: Non-executive director Devaraja Iyer Krishna Iyer resigned on 13 August 2026; Ramesh C. Behera joined as an independent director the same day. MD and whole-time director re-appointed from 31 August 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Pandyan family company from Sangli. The founder Thalavaidurai Pandyan is Chairman & MD, his son Bharanidharan Pandyan is Joint MD, and his wife Chitra Pandyan is a whole-time director. A hired CEO, Sanjog Mhatre, has run operations since February 2026. The three are proposed for re-appointment for five years from March 2027. Promoters own about 74%, most of it held by Bharanidharan.

people.name: Thalavaidurai Pandyan
people.relation: Founder; father of Joint MD Bharanidharan Pandyan and husband of whole-time director Chitra Pandyan
people.stake: 12.73% (98,60,480 shares, FY26 annual report); family together about 50%, promoter group about 74%
people.bio: Thalavaidurai Pandyan, 71, has a diploma in electrical engineering (industrial electronics) from Tamil Nadu's State Board of Technical Education. He has more than four decades of experience in high-voltage electrical equipment, power systems and power-quality products. He has been a promoter and director since the company was set up in 2001 and handles its day-to-day affairs. He is proposed for re-appointment as Chairman & MD for five years from March 2027, which needs a special resolution because he is over 70. His FY26 pay was ₹2.07cr.

people.name: Bharanidharan Pandyan
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD, Thalavaidurai Pandyan, and of Chitra Pandyan
people.bio: Bharanidharan Pandyan, 42, has an electrical and electronics engineering degree from B.M.S. College of Engineering and an MBA from S.P. Jain Institute of Management & Research, and is pursuing a PhD in strategy at S.P. Jain School of Global Management. He has more than two decades of experience in high-voltage equipment, reactors and reactive-power products, and has done business in over 95 countries. His listed expertise includes corporate strategy and mergers and acquisitions; the group has bought Endoks in Turkey, Mehru Electrical and Sukrut Electric, and plans to buy the insulator maker Win-Win. He is the largest shareholder, and his FY26 pay was ₹2.12cr.

people.name: Chitra Pandyan
people.relation: Wife of the Chairman & MD; mother of Joint MD Bharanidharan Pandyan
people.bio: Chitra Pandyan, 70, has been with the company since it was set up and oversees its administrative functions. Her listed qualification is matriculation. Her FY26 pay was ₹49.5 lakh, and she is proposed for re-appointment for five years from March 2027.

people.name: Mahesh V. Saralaya
people.since: Joined October 2006; whole-time director since February 2024
people.bio: Mahesh Saralaya, 67, has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology and is a chartered engineer registered with the Institution of Engineers (India). He joined Quality Power as a marketing manager in October 2006 and joined the board as a whole-time director in February 2024, before the IPO. He is the only non-family executive on the board.

people.name: Sanjog S. Mhatre
people.bio: Sanjog Mhatre was the company's Chief Business Officer before being made CEO in February 2026. He has more than 30 years of experience in profit-and-loss management, business turnaround and global operations, with senior roles at L&T, CTR Ltd., Arcteq and BSC GmbH. He took over the India operations when the president of India operations, Vivek Moroney, resigned at the end of December 2025.

people.name: Rajesh Jayaraman
people.bio: Rajesh Jayaraman became CFO in 2024, before the February 2025 IPO. The company describes him as experienced in finance, strategic planning, risk management and governance. Business-data profiles list earlier roles as operations director at Prager Metis Global Services, general manager for finance and investor relations at Sicagen India, general manager finance at Kare Labs, and CFO of ICE Steel 1.

companies.changes: Vivek Moroney, President & Head of India Operations, resigned on 31 December 2025. Sanjog Mhatre promoted from Chief Business Officer to CEO on 4 February 2026. No executive changes filed since the annual report (5 September 2026).

companies.styleNote: The promoter Narendra Goliya stepped back from MD to Executive Chairman in August 2024 and a hired manager, Dineshkumar Musalekar, runs the group; he was made Managing Director in May 2026. No other family member is on the board. The Goliya family and trusts own about 70%; in August 2026 a press report said they were talking to buyers, which the company did not deny.

people.name: Narendra J. Goliya
people.since: Promoter; MD until August 2024, Executive Chairman since
people.relation: Promoter; the promoter group also includes Asha, Rishabh and Anushree Goliya and two family trusts
people.stake: 42.18% (1,62,57,098 shares, held jointly with Asha Goliya, FY26 annual report); promoter group 69.55%
people.bio: Narendra Goliya has an electrical engineering degree from IIT Bombay and a master's degree in microelectronics from Stanford University. He has more than 40 years in manufacturing and the electrical industry. He built Rishabh in Nashik, bought Lumel and Lumel Alucast in Poland in July 2011, bought Sifam Tinsley in the UK and set up its US sales arm. He also runs Shanti Instruments, a company his father started in Mumbai, and chairs the Nashik Engineering Cluster. He is founder chief patron of the Jain International Trade Organisation (JITO).

people.name: Dineshkumar Musalekar
people.since: Whole-time director & Group CEO from August 2024; MD from 18 May 2026 (5 years)
people.stake: 0.52% (2,00,749 shares, FY26 annual report); also granted ESOPs
people.bio: Dineshkumar Musalekar, born in 1971, has an electronics and communications engineering degree from Karnataka University, a master's degree from the Somaiya Institute (an MBA in human resource management) and an executive programme from Henley in the UK. He spent about a decade at Otis Elevator in India, rising from graduate trainee to manager of its modernisation department, and another decade at Avire (Halma group) as India resident director and general manager for India, the Middle East and Africa. Since 2013 he has been president and CEO of the group's Polish units Lumel and Lumel Alucast, and was honoured by the mayor of Zielona Góra for turning Lumel around. He is paid ₹1.4cr in India plus salaries from both Polish units.

people.name: Vishal Kulkarni
people.bio: Vishal Kulkarni has an M.Com from Pune University and is an associate member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India. Before joining Rishabh in July 2014 he worked at Techno Force (India) and ThyssenKrupp India. He co-signs the CEO/CFO certificate on the accounts.

people.name: Mahesh Naval
people.bio: Mahesh Naval has a degree in electronics and telecommunication engineering and more than 25 years of operations experience. He previously worked at Radiant Appliances, LG, Celetronix, Globatronix and MIRC. He is listed in the annual report's management team.

people.name: Nitinkumar Deshpande
people.role: AVP – Global Head, Marketing and Strategic Business Development
people.bio: Nitinkumar Deshpande has an electrical engineering degree from Mumbai University and an MBA from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, Pune. He has more than 24 years in the electrical and electronics industry, including roles at ABB, Siemens and Schneider Electric. He leads global marketing and strategic business development.

companies.changes: Dineshkumar Musalekar re-designated from whole-time director to Managing Director on 18 May 2026 (shareholder approval at the AGM). The company disclosed Anand Laddha's resignation at a material subsidiary in July 2025. No other executive changes filed since the annual report (9 July 2026).

companies.styleNote: A subsidiary of France's Schneider Electric, which holds about 75% through Indian and Singapore holding companies. There is no family promoter; the group appoints career managers, several of them from the L&T electrical business Schneider bought in 2020. The board is chaired by an independent director, Pravin Kumar Purang, and Schneider executives sit as non-executive directors.

people.name: Udai Singh
people.since: September 2023; re-appointed for 3 years from 15 September 2026
people.stake: 500 shares (FY26 annual report); also eligible for Schneider Electric SE stock plans
people.bio: Udai Singh has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from IIT Varanasi and has attended leadership programmes at the Ross School of Business and INSEAD. He joined L&T's electrical and automation business as a graduate engineer trainee in 1992 and spent more than 33 years there and in its successor under Schneider, in sales, marketing, projects and contract management and manufacturing. His last role before this job was business head of the equipment business. He became MD & CEO in September 2023. His fixed pay plus target bonus and long-term incentive is about ₹3.8cr a year under the new term.

people.name: Soumya Bagchi
people.since: Board from 30 June 2026; whole-time director from 14 August 2026 (3 years)
people.bio: Soumya Bagchi has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Jadavpur University, Kolkata, and has attended leadership programmes at the Ross School of Business and INSEAD. He joined L&T's electrical and automation business as a graduate engineer trainee in 1994 and moved to Schneider when it bought that business in 2020. Over more than 30 years he has handled profit-and-loss ownership, product development, business development, projects and manufacturing. He was business unit head for medium-voltage equipment and earlier headed project and contract management for low- and medium-voltage equipment in India, the Middle East and Africa. He joined the board as whole-time director Chinmoy Das was leaving.

people.name: Omkar Prasad
people.bio: Omkar Prasad is a fellow chartered accountant with a master's degree in economics, is an alumnus of IIM Bangalore and holds certifications in business responsibility and sustainability reporting. Before becoming CFO he was Schneider Electric's chief accounting officer for Greater India, covering India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. He has more than two decades in financial control, tax compliance, risk management and digital finance projects, and earlier worked as plant controller, internal auditor and corporate finance manager. He replaced Suparna Banerjee Bhattacharyya, who left to pursue a career outside the group.

companies.changes: CFO Suparna Banerjee Bhattacharyya left on 15 September 2025; Omkar Prasad took over the next day. Whole-time director Chinmoy Das resigned for personal reasons with effect from 30 June 2026; Soumya Bagchi joined the board on 30 June and became whole-time director on 14 August 2026. Udai Singh re-appointed MD & CEO from 15 September 2026.

companies.styleNote: Keyur Shah took over the company as managing director in 2008 and is Chairman & MD; his wife Twinkle Shah is a non-executive director. Day-to-day functions are run by hired executive directors for finance, global business and operations, who are not board members. A German bushing expert, Hartmuth Fethke, sits as a non-executive director. The couple own about 55% (53.4% and 1.9% at March 2026).

people.name: Keyur G. Shah
people.relation: Promoter; husband of non-executive director Twinkle Shah
people.stake: 53.36% (1,52,34,595 shares, FY26 annual report); with his wife about 55%
people.bio: Keyur Shah has a diploma in civil engineering from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. He joined Yash Highvoltage in March 2008, when he took it over as managing director, and has about 25 years of industry experience. He built it into what the company calls India's leading maker of high-voltage and high-current transformer bushings, and chairs its technical advisory board. At the 2024 IPO he oversaw administration and finance. His other ventures include Yash Swisstech, Desar Estate and Upscale Developers. Shareholders are being asked to approve pay above the statutory limit for him from March 2026.

people.name: Darshan Thakkar
people.bio: Darshan Thakkar has more than 25 years in finance, mostly at banks including Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, ABN AMRO and The Royal Bank of Scotland, before moving into corporate finance at manufacturers. He heads finance and accounts and also oversees investor relations, risk management, legal and compliance, HR and IT. He is not a board director; 'executive director' is his job title.

people.name: Sumit Poddar
people.bio: Sumit Poddar has cleared the final examination of the Institute of Cost and Works Accountants of India. He has about 25 years of experience across pharma and life sciences, oil and rubber, metals and mining, procurement, project finance and investment banking. He joined Yash in September 2022 and became CFO in August 2024, before the IPO. He advises the MD on finance, planning and investment decisions.

people.name: Nirav P. Patel
people.bio: Nirav Patel is an electrical engineer and has completed a HarvardX online course in entrepreneurship in emerging economies. He has more than 18 years in operations, marketing and business leadership in the power and manufacturing sectors, rising at Yash through roles as assistant manager for sales and marketing, general manager for business operations and chief marketing officer. He leads international business, sales and marketing, and represents the company on the Central Electricity Authority and Bureau of Indian Standards committees for transformer bushings.

people.name: Gautam R. Nikam
people.bio: Gautam Nikam has a diploma in electrical engineering from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. He has more than 14 years in the power industry, with expertise in bushing design, manufacturing and testing. He runs plant operations and the technology function and plans capital spending.

companies.changes: Company Secretary Tushar Lakhmapurkar (at the IPO) has been replaced by Bhoomi Talati, named in the FY26 annual report. No change in the CMD or CFO.

companies.styleNote: A Shah family company from Vadodara, founded by the late Jitendra Shah. His son Alay Shah is Chairman & MD, and Alay's sons Aashay and Aatman Shah are whole-time directors (Aatman since March 2026). The family owns about 62%, including Shilpa Alay Shah and the family HUF. Family pay was about ₹11cr in FY26, with Alay Shah alone at ₹8.3cr.

people.name: Alay J. Shah
people.since: Promoter director since incorporation (employment from November 1988); MD term to September 2027
people.relation: Son of the late founder Jitendra Shah; father of whole-time directors Aashay and Aatman Shah
people.stake: 23.68% (27,09,548 shares, FY26 annual report; sold 1.9% during the year); family together 62.12%
people.bio: Alay Shah, 60, has a bachelor's degree in science with a specialisation in electronics. He has been a promoter director since the company was incorporated and has more than 33 years of experience across production, finance, marketing and administration. The board credits his day-to-day involvement for the rise in turnover and has asked shareholders to approve higher pay for him; his FY26 pay was ₹8.3cr. He chairs the CSR committee and attends audit committee meetings as an invitee. He is also a director of AJShah Enterprise.

people.name: Aashay A. Shah
people.since: Director since November 2021; re-appointed for 5 years from November 2026 (subject to approval)
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD, Alay Shah; brother of Aatman Shah
people.bio: Aashay Shah, 35, has a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and an MBA from Cass Business School, London. He joined the company in January 2014 and was manager of operations until August 2016, covering marketing, production, procurement and design. He has handled business development since October 2017 and chairs the risk management committee. His FY26 pay was ₹1.5cr.

people.name: Aatman A. Shah
people.since: Joined November 2016; whole-time director from 6 March 2026
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD, Alay Shah; brother of Aashay Shah
people.bio: Aatman Shah, 32, has a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. He was manager of operations from November 2016 to June 2022, covering marketing, production, procurement and design, and has handled business development since June 2022. Shareholders approved his appointment as a whole-time director by postal ballot in March 2026.

people.name: Prajesh K. Purohit
people.bio: Prajesh Purohit is the CFO and a key managerial person, and signs the CEO/CFO certificate with the MD. The annual report and website give no details of his education or earlier career.

companies.changes: Aatman Shah became a whole-time director on 6 March 2026. No executive changes filed since the annual report (11 August 2026). The website lists Anand Bhanpurkar as COO, with no background given.

companies.styleNote: Founder Kunhamed Bicha is Chairman & MD and the only executive on the board; the board has re-appointed him for five more years from July 2027. Co-promoter Bhaskar Srinivasan sold part of his stake in 2025 and left the board in February 2026. Finance and operations are run by hired professionals. There are no family ties among the directors. Promoters own about 44%.

people.name: Kunhamed Bicha
people.since: 1999 (with the company since incorporation); Chairman & MD since July 2022
people.relation: Founder and promoter
people.stake: 21.61% (FY26 annual report); the KL Bicha Family Private Trust holds another 9.39%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from PSG College of Technology and a master's in industrial engineering from Wichita State University, USA. He has been with Avalon since it was set up in 1999 and has led its growth from circuit-board assembly into complete box-build systems for global customers. He has been Chairman & MD since July 2022, and in September 2026 the board approved his re-appointment for five years from July 2027. The Confederation of Indian Industry named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Manufacturing) in 2017.

people.name: Suresh Veerappan
people.since: CFO (KMP) as of the FY26 annual report
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a Global Executive MBA in leadership and strategy from the Indian School of Business. He has more than 19 years of experience in business strategy, investor relations, financial modelling, working capital, audit, M&A and compliance. Before Avalon he worked with Bank of America, State Bank of India and Grant Thornton. He runs finance for the company and its subsidiaries, and wrote the FY26 shareholder letter describing the finance automation work done during the year.

people.name: Shriram Vijayaraghavan
people.since: COO as of the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Responsible for overall operations of Avalon and its subsidiaries. He holds a BE in mechanical engineering from SVCE (Anna University, Chennai), an MS in mechanical engineering from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and an MBA from the Kellogg School of Management. Earlier he was President at Wheels India, a Vice President at Hertz Corporation in the US and an Engagement Manager at McKinsey & Co in the US. He also co-contributed to research at Caterpillar and the University of Michigan.

companies.changes: Co-promoter Bhaskar Srinivasan resigned from the board on 10 February 2026. R M Subramanian, previously Avalon's Group CFO, left and joined Cyient DLM as CFO in October 2025. In September 2026 the board approved Kunhamed Bicha's re-appointment as Chairman & MD for five years from 12 July 2027 (subject to shareholders).

companies.styleNote: Controlled by Cyient Ltd (about 52%), but run by a hired MD & CEO. Krishna Bodanapu (Cyient's Executive Vice-Chairman and MD) is the non-executive chairman, and his father B.V.R. Mohan Reddy, founder of Cyient, is a non-executive director. Neither holds an executive role here.

people.name: Rajendra Velagapudi
people.since: On the board since April 2017; CEO from July 2025; MD & CEO
people.stake: 2,882 shares, a negligible stake (FY26 AGM notice)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering and two master's degrees in engineering and design, from the Madras Institute of Technology, Chennai and Cranfield University, UK. He has about 38 years of engineering and manufacturing experience, starting at Simpson & Co., Bajaj Tempo and Bharat Earth Movers before joining Cyient in 1999. At Cyient he was President & Chief Business Officer and Operations Head of Engineering Services. He has been with the DLM business since 2017 and became CEO in July 2025, replacing Anthony Montalbano; he runs the electronics and mechanical manufacturing units globally. He sits on the governing or advisory bodies of three engineering colleges.

people.name: R M Subramanian
people.bio: An engineer from BITS Pilani and an alumnus of IIM Bangalore, with over 25 years of experience across EMS, energy, manufacturing and consulting. Just before joining he was Group CFO of Avalon Technologies, overseeing corporate finance, reporting, controls, tax and secretarial work. Earlier finance roles include the Sanmar group, Cairn India and Essar Oil. He replaced Shrinivas Kulkarni, who moved to a role within the Cyient group.

people.name: Kaushal Jadia
people.since: CTO (senior management) as of the FY26 annual report
people.bio: Has over 30 years of experience. He holds a master's in communication and radar engineering from IIT Delhi and a bachelor's in electrical engineering from the Naval College of Engineering. Before Cyient DLM he was with Cyient Ltd, and for six years with Airbus Defence and Space, where he led its captive engineering centre in Bengaluru and was CTO of L&T Cassidian, the Airbus DS–L&T joint venture. At Cyient DLM he leads technology for aerospace, defence, RF and electronic-warfare work.

people.name: Ramakanth Alapati
people.role: President & Chief Strategy and Growth Officer
people.bio: Has more than 20 years of experience in advanced semiconductor packaging, foundry operations, capital equipment and deep-tech manufacturing. He chairs the 3DIC Technical Advisory Board at Sematech and the Packaging Technical Advisory Board at the Semiconductor Research Corporation. He holds an MS in chemical engineering from the University of Kansas and a bachelor's in engineering from Osmania University, Hyderabad. He joined as senior management in May 2026 to lead strategy and growth.

companies.changes: CFO Shrinivas Kulkarni stepped down on 24 October 2025 (moved within the Cyient group); R M Subramanian took over. Head of Operations Mujeeb Rahiman resigned with effect from 30 April 2026. Rajendra Velagapudi replaced Anthony Montalbano as CEO from 1 July 2025. Ramakanth Alapati joined as President & Chief Strategy and Growth Officer on 18 May 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Apparao Mallavarapu is Chairman & MD and his son Nikhil is Joint MD. His daughter Tanya sits on the board as a non-executive director. The promoter family owns about 47%; a hired CFO runs finance.

people.name: Apparao Mallavarapu
people.since: 1993 (founder); re-appointed for five years from August 2025
people.relation: Founder; father of Joint MD Nikhil Mallavarapu and director Tanya Mallavarapu
people.stake: 35.49% (FY26 annual report); promoter family together about 47%
people.bio: Founded Centum in 1993 and has led it into a defence, space and aerospace electronics design and manufacturing company, including joint ventures with several global multinationals. He holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Bangalore University and a master's from Dalhousie University, Canada, and completed the Harvard Business School Presidential Program; he is a Ford Foundation scholar. He chairs the CII National Committee on Space and is Honorary Consul of Brazil in Bengaluru. He sold 6.66 lakh shares (about 4.5% of the company) in August 2025.

people.name: Nikhil Mallavarapu
people.since: With Centum since August 2012; Whole-time Director until May 2025, then Joint MD
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD; brother of director Tanya Mallavarapu
people.bio: Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical and computer engineering from Carnegie Mellon University and an MBA from INSEAD. Before Centum he worked with Analog Devices in its MEMS sensors division. He joined Centum in August 2012 and was re-designated from Whole-time Director to Joint MD in 2025; he wrote his first shareholder letter in that role in the FY26 annual report. He is on the executive council of the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers and is a YPO member.

people.name: Sundararajan Parthasarathy
people.bio: A chartered accountant and commerce graduate from the University of Madras, with over 24 years in healthcare, automotive, energy infrastructure, water technology, HR services and green energy. Before Centum he was the first Global CFO of Agratas, the Tata group's battery venture, from January 2022 to January 2024, helping set up its greenfield projects in India and the UK. He succeeded K.S. Desikan, who retired after more than two decades as CFO.

people.name: Vinod Chippalkatti
people.since: CTO from January 2026 (earlier President, Strategic Electronics)
people.bio: A former ISRO scientist with an engineering degree in electrical, electronics and communications from NITK Surathkal (per Bloomberg and his public profiles). His expertise is DC-DC power converters and space electronics, and he earlier headed Centum's Strategic Electronics business unit as its President. The company re-designated him Chief Technology Officer from 1 January 2026.

companies.changes: CFO K.S. Desikan retired on 31 August 2025; Sundararajan Parthasarathy took over from 1 September 2025. Vinod Chippalkatti was re-designated CTO from 1 January 2026. No executive changes found after the FY26 annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founder Narendra Narayanan is Chairman & MD and his son Sumukh Narendra is a whole-time director. His wife Meera Narendra, a co-founder and promoter, is not on the board. Long-time operations head T.R. Srinivasan is the third executive director. The family owns about 29%.

people.name: Narendra Narayanan
people.relation: Founder; father of Sumukh Narendra; husband of co-founder Meera Narendra
people.stake: about 18.5% (23,29,002 shares, FY26 annual report); family together 29.4%
people.bio: Holds a master's in electrical and electronics engineering from the University of Southern California. He set up Vinyas in 2000–01 to build a global Indian electronics manufacturing business, and has grown it into a design-and-manufacture company serving defence, aerospace and export customers. He has served as chairman and adviser to other companies and sits on the India advisory board of USC's Viterbi School of Engineering. The company received the National Trust's Best Employer award (2011–12) for hiring people with disabilities, and he received USC's Widney House Volunteer Award in 2014.

people.name: Sumukh Narendra
people.relation: Son of the Chairman & MD Narendra Narayanan and of co-founder Meera Narendra
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in electronics and communication engineering from Sri Jayachamarajendra College of Engineering, Mysuru, and a master's in embedded systems engineering from the University of Pennsylvania. Before joining Vinyas he worked as a lead design engineer at Fortune 100 multinationals in the US, mainly on diagnostic and digital healthcare products. At Vinyas since 2018, he has driven expansion into Europe in medical, power electronics and industrial work, and Industry 4.0 projects. He is a member of CII's Mysore chapter.

people.name: T.R. Srinivasan
people.bio: Holds a diploma in mechanical engineering from Karnataka's Department of Technical Education. He joined Vinyas in 2001 and has spent over two decades in electronics manufacturing and hardware. He oversees the whole manufacturing facility and built the company's manufacturing team. He held 48,000 shares at the time of the 2023 IPO.

people.name: Amitava Majumdar
people.bio: A cost and management accountant with about 36 years of experience at the time of the 2023 IPO. He spent more than three decades in senior finance roles at Indian and multinational companies in automobiles, FMCG, pharmaceuticals and engineering. His work covers financial reporting, internal and budgetary controls, systems implementation and fund raising. The prospectus does not name his earlier employers.

companies.changes: No executive changes found since the FY26 annual report. Sumukh Narendra retires by rotation and seeks re-appointment at the 2026 AGM.

people.name: Mukesh Jeram Vasani
people.since: On the board since October 2013; Managing Director from 1 August 2026 to July 2031
people.relation: Promoter; father of director Nirmal Vasani
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from Sardar Patel University, Gujarat (1987), and has over three decades in production, marketing and manufacturing of engineering and electronic products. US companies under the same management, such as Aimtron Corporation and American Pinball, both buy from and sell to Aimtron. He joined the board in 2013 and was non-executive Chairman until shareholders approved him as Managing Director for five years at the August 2026 AGM. His FY26 chairman's letter highlighted the purchase of International Control Services in Illinois (now Aimtron International Controls) and the new Vadodara plant.

people.name: Sharmilaben Lakhanbhai Bambhaniya
people.since: Whole-time Director (on the board at the 2024 IPO)
people.relation: Promoter; mother-in-law of director Nirmal Vasani (son of the Chairman)

people.bio: Holds a B.Com (1993) and M.Com (1995) from colleges in Rajkot and a law degree (2010) from S.S. Ajmera Municipal Law College, Gondal. She has about two decades of experience in social work, education advisory and business management. At Aimtron she oversees the finance and administrative functions.

people.name: Sneh Shah
people.bio: An electronics engineer with about a decade in the electronics industry; he is a certified PMP, a Chartered Engineer and a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt. He leads sales, customer growth and project delivery, and wrote a shareholder letter in the FY26 annual report for the first time. He was an allottee in the 2024 pre-IPO share issue.

people.name: Nikita Shah
people.bio: Holds a Master of Commerce in accounting and financial management from the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2010). She joined Aimtron in 2021 as a senior accounts executive and was made CFO in October 2023, before the IPO. She handles the company's overall finances. The prospectus gives no earlier employers.

people.name: Jaidit Singh Brar

He holds an MBA from IIM Calcutta and an honours degree in economics from Punjab University. He has served as an independent director on the boards of Exide Industries and Tenneco Clean Air. people.name: Bijay Kumar Agrawal

people.bio: Has over 22 years in finance, covering corporate finance, treasury, M&A, business strategy and financial risk management. He previously worked at Dalmia Bharat, Times Internet and Motorola India. The annual report does not give his qualifications.

people.name: Jayesh Nagindas Doshi

people.name: Krishna Kumar Pant

people.name: Ranjit Singh Lonial

people.name: Ramesh Kunhikannan

people.relation: Promoter; wife of founder Ramesh Kunhikannan

people.name: Dr Muthukumar Narayanaswamy

At Kaynes he is leading the ramp-up of the Sanand chip-packaging and Chennai circuit-board plants and a push to cut working-capital days.

people.name: Jairam Paravastu Sampath
people.since: With Kaynes since 2011; board since March 2018; Whole-time Director since April 2022, re-appointed from April 2027

In the FY26 annual report he set a target of cutting the cash conversion cycle from 125 days to 100 days by FY28.

He has chaired the Board of Governors of Government Engineering College, Bhavnagar, since 2014, and is an independent director of Mukesh Babu Financial Services. He is 66.

people.name: Rushil C. Tamboli
people.relation: Son of Chairman & MD Chetan Tamboli; brother of director Vidhi Merchant
people.stake: 0.49% (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); he received the shares from within the family during the year
people.bio: A graduate in industrial engineering from Pennsylvania State University, USA. He joined Steelcast as a management trainee in August 2011 and rose to whole-time director. He ran a Six Sigma project to cut fuel use in heat treatment, headed the heat-treatment section and the shell-moulding foundry, and helped develop new parts and cut man-hours per tonne. He now co-manages day-to-day operations with his father.

people.name: Ashutosh H. Shukla
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from M.S. University with a postgraduate diploma in business administration. He has 37 years of experience across several firms and has been with Steelcast since 1997. He runs operations at all the plants and also heads human resources. He joined the board as an executive director in January 2023 for five years. He is 63.

people.name: Subhash R. Sharma
people.bio: Holds a master's in commerce, is a cost accountant (ICMAI) and a qualified company secretary. He joined Steelcast in 2016 and is CFO, handling bank finance, audits, accounts and investor meetings. He also oversees secretarial work, stores, administration and security. He became an executive director in January 2023 for five years. He is 60.

companies.changes: No change in directors or KMP since the annual report. The board re-appointed Chetan Tamboli as MD for five years from 1 Sep 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: Founded in 1978 by Bhadresh Shah, who owns 58.47% and has been Chairman & MD since the non-executive chairman Rajendra Shah stepped down in April 2026. His daughters Khushali Solanki and Bhumika Shodhan sit on the board as non-executive directors. A long-serving whole-time director and a hired CFO complete the executive team. Promoters own 58.49%.

people.name: Bhadresh K. Shah
people.since: Founder (1978); MD; Chairman since 21 April 2026; re-appointed MD to September 2031
people.relation: Founder; father of non-executive directors Khushali Solanki and Bhumika Shodhan
people.stake: 58.47% (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); promoter group together 58.49%
people.bio: Holds a B.Tech in metallurgy from IIT Kanpur. He set up the business in 1978 as Ahmedabad Induction Alloys and has over 55 years in making high-chrome wear-resistant castings such as grinding media, mill liners, diaphragms and vertical-mill parts for the cement, thermal power and mining industries. He built AIA into a global supplier, listed in 2005, with a focus on process improvement, new products and international quality standards. He became Chairman in April 2026, and shareholders re-appointed him MD for five years from 1 October 2026.

people.name: Yashwant M. Patel
people.bio: A science graduate (B.Sc., chemistry) with long experience in production, administration, human resources and accounts. He has been a whole-time director since November 2010. The company says he chaired CII Gujarat in 2012–13 and sits on the endowment committee of IIT Gandhinagar. He is an independent director of Ratnamani Metals & Tubes. He is 82 and is not related to any other director.

people.name: Viren K. Thakkar
people.bio: A chartered accountant. Before joining AIA he was CFO of GTPL Hathway, the cable-TV and broadband company. He became AIA's CFO and a key managerial person in August 2019.

people.name: Kunal D. Shah
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from Nirma Institute of Technology and an M.S. in information systems from Stevens Institute of Technology, USA. He has been with AIA since December 2002 and heads corporate affairs as a senior manager (not a board member). He is also an independent director of Harsha Engineers, founding trustee of The Lightship Initiative, and has his own consulting firm, Theoden Ventures.

companies.changes: Chairman Rajendra Shah (non-executive) resigned on 20 Apr 2026 and Bhadresh Shah became Chairman. Executive Director (Commercial) B. F. Shah resigned on 17 Mar 2026. Shareholders re-appointed Bhadresh Shah as MD at the 15 Sep 2026 AGM.

companies.styleNote: A Garg-family company started in Ludhiana in 1979 making forged bicycle pedals. Founder Paritosh Kumar is Chairman & MD, his son Ashish Garg is MD and runs the business day to day, and Ashish's wife Megha Garg is a whole-time director. Hired professionals run finance, plants and marketing. The family owns about 78.5%, most of it through the Garg Family Trust (40.33%).

people.name: Paritosh Kumar
people.relation: Founder; father of MD Ashish Garg; father-in-law of Whole-time Director Megha Garg
people.stake: 9.49% (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); the Paritosh Kumar (Garg Family Trust) holds 40.33% and his HUF 0.73%; promoter group together about 78.5%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in arts from S.C. Dhawan Government Evening College, Punjab University. He has over 45 years in the industry and started the business in Ludhiana in 1979 making forged bicycle pedals. He oversees operations, capital allocation, expansion and governance.

people.name: Ashish Garg
people.relation: Son of Chairman Paritosh Kumar; husband of Whole-time Director Megha Garg
people.stake: 13.72% (31 Mar 2026, FY26 annual report); Ashish Garg & Sons (HUF) holds 0.27%
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. in accounting and finance and an M.Sc. in manufacturing systems engineering from the University of Warwick, UK. He has about 19 years in the industry. As MD he leads business operations, financial performance, growth strategy, investments and product development, including the move to 8,000- and 14,000-tonne presses for larger industrial forgings.

people.name: Megha Garg
people.since: Whole-time Director since September 2021; board re-appointed her to September 2031
people.relation: Wife of MD Ashish Garg; daughter-in-law of Chairman Paritosh Kumar
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. in economics from the University of Nottingham, UK, and has about 10 years in the industry. She is responsible for digital marketing, customer engagement and ESG. The board re-appointed her for five years from 29 September 2026, subject to shareholder approval.

people.name: Pankaj Kumar Goyal
people.bio: A commerce graduate and fellow chartered accountant (ICAI) with 24 years of finance experience in manufacturing. He has been with Happy Forgings since 2013 and handles financial strategy, reporting, fundraising, capital allocation, risk and tax.

people.name: Narinder Singh Juneja
people.bio: Holds a postgraduate diploma in mechanical engineering (machine tools operation and maintenance) from YMCA Institute of Engineering, Haryana. He has over five decades of industrial experience and oversees manufacturing processes.

people.name: Patwinder Singh
people.bio: Holds a B.Sc. from Guru Nanak Dev University and an MBA from CSM Institute of Graduate Studies, with 30 years in operations and marketing. Since joining in 2016 he has run production and operations at one of the plants.

people.name: Mangesh Shantaram Purandare
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering and an MBA from the University of Pune, with nearly 30 years of marketing in auto components. Since joining in 2019 he has led new business development in India and abroad.

companies.changes: No change in directors or KMP since the annual report. The board re-appointed Megha Garg as whole-time director from 29 Sep 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
