He has a science degree and an MBA from Mumbai University, a diploma in entrepreneurship management, and completed the ISB-Kellogg Global Advanced Management Programme. He has 40-plus years in finance, operations, purchase, projects and international business, and is responsible for formulation manufacturing, supply chain, finance and the international business. He won the CFO 100 'Winning Edge in Cost Management' award in 2011 and 2012.

people.name: Pramod Ghorpade
people.role: Chief Financial Officer (President, Finance & Group CFO)
people.bio: Pramod Ghorpade is a chartered accountant and Indoco's Group CFO. Before Indoco he was India country CFO at the Teva group and held finance roles at Watson Pharmaceuticals, including Controller for India.

people.name: Dr. Kavita Inamdar
people.bio: Dr. Kavita Inamdar is Chief Technical Officer and is listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report. Her remit matters as the Goa sterile plants await a US FDA re-inspection.

people.name: Rajesh Usgaonker
people.bio: Rajesh Usgaonker heads Indian sales and marketing, taking over from Ajay Karajagi, who retired in November 2025. He is listed as senior management in the FY26 annual report.

people.name: Ramanathan Hariharan
people.bio: Ramanathan Hariharan is Company Secretary, Compliance Officer and Head of Legal, and a key managerial person.

companies.changes: Ajay Karajagi (President, Sales & Marketing) retired on 30 Nov 2025. Sudhir Kadam joined as Senior Vice President, Human Capital, on 28 Jul 2026. Aditi Panandikar re-appointed MD from 15 Feb 2027, subject to shareholder approval. In FY26 the Kare family moved shares into a new Kare Family Private Trust (14.2%).

companies.styleNote: The Dhanuka group bought Orchid out of insolvency and runs it. Manish Dhanuka is MD and Mridul Dhanuka is Whole-time Director. Dhanuka group founder Ram Gopal Agarwal is non-executive Chairman, and promoter Arjun Dhanuka (4.8%) is a non-executive director. The annual report says the board members are not relatives of each other under company law. Dhanuka Laboratories, the promoters' own company, merged into Orchid on 10 July 2026. The promoter group owns about 69.8%.

people.name: Manish Dhanuka
people.relation: Promoter (Dhanuka group)
people.stake: 10.94% (FY26 annual report, including shares allotted under the Dhanuka Laboratories merger); promoter group about 69.8%
people.bio: Manish Dhanuka is Orchid's Managing Director. He has a B.Tech in chemical engineering from IIT Delhi and an MS in chemical engineering from the University of Akron in the US. He has more than 30 years of experience in pharmaceutical research, operations, commercial, marketing and finance. In his FY26 letter he framed the July 2026 merger of the promoters' Dhanuka Laboratories into Orchid as giving the company control of its chain from starting materials to finished sterile medicine. His personal guarantee backs part of the working-capital loans. The FY25 annual report said he held no Orchid shares directly; his stake came through the merger.

people.name: Mridul Dhanuka
people.relation: Promoter group (Dhanuka family)
people.stake: 0.54% via Mridul Dhanuka HUF (FY26 annual report)
people.bio: Mridul Dhanuka is a chemical engineer with an MBA and has been with the Dhanuka group since 2005. The company credits him with expanding the group's production capacity, building a new manufacturing plant and reorganising the supply chain from buying to selling. He is described as the driving force behind the company's new business line.

people.name: Sunil Kumar Gupta
people.bio: Sunil Kumar Gupta is CFO and a key managerial person, and signs the financial statements with the MD. The annual reports do not give his background.

people.name: Kapil Dayya
people.bio: Kapil Dayya is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer and a key managerial person, as listed in the FY26 annual report.

companies.changes: No director or KMP changes found in FY26 or since the annual report. The Dhanuka Laboratories merger took effect on 10 July 2026, raising the promoters' direct holdings.

companies.styleNote: A family company run by the Medhoras. Co-founder Dr. Daulat Medhora, 81, is Chairperson and Joint MD, and her son Fredun Medhora is MD and also CFO, so there is no separate finance head. Co-founder Nariman Medhora died in June 2025. Promoters own about 44.6% (July 2026).

people.name: Fredun Nariman Medhora
people.relation: Son of co-founders Dr. Daulat Medhora and the late Nariman Medhora
people.bio: Fredun Medhora has been on the board since October 2014 and is both Managing Director and CFO. He has a business entrepreneurship degree, magna cum laude, from Plattsburgh University in New York, and an MBA from Cardiff Business School in Wales, where his thesis was on India's nutraceuticals industry. He is also a director of the family companies Fredun Healthcare, Fredna Enterprises and Trois Biotech. He was paid ₹54 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Dr. Daulat N. Medhora
people.relation: Co-founder; widow of Nariman Medhora; mother of the MD
people.stake: 25.78% (FY26 annual report); a further 13.15% is still held in the late Nariman Medhora's name
people.bio: Dr. Daulat Medhora, 81, has been a director since June 1987. She has a master's and a PhD in chemistry from UDCT Mumbai and won the Lady Tata Scholarship for her research. She began as an R&D manager and was approved by the FDA as expert staff in fine chemicals, developing processes for several drugs and intermediates. In 1994 she and her husband set up Fredun's export-oriented plant at Palghar. She retires by rotation at the 2026 AGM and is up for re-appointment; she was paid ₹12 lakh in FY26.

people.name: Vaishnavi Rajkamal Sahu
people.bio: Vaishnavi Sahu became Company Secretary and Compliance Officer on 28 November 2025, replacing Parag Goyal. She is a key managerial person.

companies.changes: Co-founder and director Nariman Medhora died on 20 Jun 2025. Company Secretary Parag Goyal resigned on 26 Nov 2025 and Vaishnavi Sahu replaced him. Three new independent directors joined in 2025. Promoter warrants were converted in FY26 and again in September 2026.

companies.styleNote: China's Fosun Pharma controls the company through Fosun Pharma Industrial Pte, which owns 51.8% (June 2026). Fosun sits on the board only through non-executive directors; the business is run by hired managers, led by Executive Chairman Srinivas Sadu. The founding Raju/Penmetsa family no longer runs it.

people.name: Srinivas Sadu
people.bio: Holds a master's in industrial pharmacy from Long Island University (New York), an MBA from the University of Maryland, and a postgraduate certificate in finance and management from the London School of Business and Finance. Before Gland he was a product manager and business lead at Natco Pharma and a product manager in consumer health at SmithKline Beecham. He joined Gland in 2000, became Chief Operating Officer in 2011 and Managing Director & CEO in 2019, and moved up to Executive Chairman in January 2025. He has worked on business development, manufacturing, supply chain and strategy for over two decades, and is the long-serving face of the company to investors.

people.name: Deepak Sapra
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from the Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Jamalpur, with a management degree from IIM Bangalore; he was a Chevening Scholar at the University of Bradford and a Fulbright Fellow at Carnegie Mellon. He has about 27 years of executive experience, over 23 of them in pharma. Most recently he was CEO of API and Services at Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, running a business-to-business unit spanning generics, contract manufacturing (CDMO) and active ingredients, and sat on the board of Aurigene Pharma Services. He fills the CEO seat left empty since the previous CEO left at the end of April 2026.

people.name: Ravi Shekhar Mitra
people.bio: A qualified chartered accountant and company secretary who also completed the General Management Program at the Wharton School. He has more than 20 years of experience in financial management, planning, strategy and investor relations in pharma and related industries. He joined Gland as CFO in 2019, a year before its 2020 stock-market listing, and has stayed in the role since.

companies.changes: CEO Shyamakant Giri resigned in Feb 2026 and left on 30 Apr 2026; Deepak Sapra (ex-Dr. Reddy's) was named CEO in Aug 2026 and joins on 16 Nov 2026. COO Satnam Singh Loomba retired on 31 Mar 2026.

companies.styleNote: A family business: founder Ashok Kumar Windlass is a whole-time director and his sons Hitesh (MD) and Manoj (Joint MD) run the company, alongside a hired CEO & CFO, Komal Gupta. Hitesh's wife Prachi Jain Windlass is a non-executive director. The board chairman, Vivek Dhariwal, is independent. Promoters own 63.3% (June 2026), mostly through the AKW WBL Family Private Trust (40.6%).

people.name: Hitesh Windlass
people.relation: Son of founder Ashok Kumar Windlass; brother of Joint MD Manoj Kumar Windlass; husband of director Prachi Jain Windlass
people.stake: Under 0.01% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); family and family trust together 63.3%
people.bio: Worked as a process engineer at Intel Corporation in the US before joining the family business. He has about 18 years of management experience at Windlas. He set up the domestic trade-generics, over-the-counter brands and export businesses, and drives technical operations, quality, manufacturing and financial strategy. The board re-appointed him MD from 30 April 2025 for five years.

people.name: Manoj Kumar Windlass
people.relation: Son of founder Ashok Kumar Windlass; brother of MD Hitesh Windlass
people.stake: Under 0.01% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); family and family trust together 63.3%
people.bio: Has over 20 years of experience in product development, operations, procurement and portfolio management. He set up the contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) services and products division, which is the company's main business. The board re-appointed him Joint MD from 30 April 2025 for five years.

people.name: Ashok Kumar Windlass
people.relation: Founder; father of Hitesh and Manoj Kumar Windlass
people.stake: 21.3% (June 2026 shareholding pattern); family and family trust together 63.3%
people.bio: The founder and promoter of the company. He oversees administration, legal matters and engineering. He is a former chairman of the Confederation of Indian Industry's Uttarakhand State Council and received the Uttarakhand Ratan award in 2018. He is also a director of group companies Windlas Exports and Ashok Vimla Trusteeship Services, the trustee of the family trust that holds the largest block of shares. Shareholders approved his re-appointment as whole-time director from 3 May 2026.

people.name: Komal Gupta
people.role: Chief Executive Officer & Chief Financial Officer
people.bio: A chartered accountant, company secretary and cost accountant with nearly 20 years in strategy, finance, operations and supply chain. Before Windlas she worked at the Anand Automotive group (Perfect Circle India, Anand Automotive Systems) and at DSM Sinochem Pharmaceuticals India. She joined Windlas as CFO and was promoted to CEO in February 2023 after more than seven years with the company, keeping the CFO job as well. She was named CII Young CFO of the Year in 2023 and is on the CFO100 Roll of Honour for 2025.

people.name: Pawan Kumar Sharma
people.bio: Has more than 25 years of experience in the pharma industry. As executive director he manages the company's legal, commercial and administrative work. He holds no directorship or full-time role in any other company.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the annual report. Komal Gupta has held both the CEO and CFO jobs since Feb 2023; the company said then it would hire a separate CFO, but has not named one.

companies.styleNote: Founder Dr. D. R. Rao is Executive Chairman and his two sons run the company: Saharsh is CEO & MD (since spring 2026) and Sucheth is Executive Vice Chairman. The CFO and other function heads are hired professionals. Promoters own about 32.6% (June 2026), mostly through the Davuluri Ownership Trust (26.0%), whose trustees are the father and both sons.

people.name: Dr. Davuluri Rama Mohan Rao
people.relation: Founder; father of Sucheth and Saharsh Davuluri
people.stake: 1.6% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also a trustee of the Davuluri Ownership Trust (26.0%); family together about 32.6%
people.bio: Holds a master's in science from Andhra University, a postgraduate diploma in technology from IIT Kharagpur and a PhD in organic chemistry from the University of Notre Dame (US). He held senior research, production and quality roles at Glaxo India and was later director of R&D and quality at another drug company. He founded Neuland in 1984. He is a member of the Royal Society of Chemistry.

people.name: Davuluri Saharsh Rao
people.relation: Son of the Executive Chairman; younger brother of Executive Vice Chairman Sucheth
people.stake: 1.5% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also a trustee of the Davuluri Ownership Trust (26.0%)
people.bio: An electrical engineering graduate with a master's in management information systems from the Weatherhead School of Management (Cleveland) and an MBA from the University of North Carolina. He worked in sales roles at Sify before joining Neuland in 2007. He started the custom manufacturing (contract work for innovators) business, which is now the company's largest, and oversaw marketing, IT, business development and R&D. He took over as CEO & MD in 2026, saying the aim is to be one of the world's top five ingredient-focused CDMOs within a decade.

people.name: Davuluri Sucheth Rao
people.relation: Son of the Executive Chairman; elder brother of CEO & MD Saharsh
people.stake: 2.0% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also a trustee of the Davuluri Ownership Trust (26.0%)
people.bio: A mechanical engineer with an MBA in corporate finance and operations from the University of Notre Dame's Mendoza College of Business, and a Six Sigma Black Belt. He joined in 2002 and was chief executive from 2009 until March 2026, when he handed the role to his brother and became Executive Vice Chairman. He is on the board of the US industry body DCAT (third vice president for 2026) and is an executive member of YPO's Hyderabad chapter.

people.name: Abhijit Majumdar
people.bio: A chartered accountant and cost accountant with more than 30 years in finance. He worked at Asian Paints PPG, Berger Paints and Tata Steel, and his last job before Neuland was EVP, financial planning and controlling, at Deepak Fertilizers and Petrochemicals. His areas are accounting, working capital, tax and mergers. The board appointed him CFO in November 2022.

people.name: Dr. Sharadsrikar Venkatesan Kotturi
people.bio: Has BSc (Tech) and MSc (Tech) degrees from UDCT Bombay and a PhD from Oklahoma State University (2002), followed by medicinal chemistry research at the Research Triangle Institute in North Carolina. He has about 20 years in drug research. Before Neuland he was Senior Vice President, Operations at Piramal Pharma and held roles at GVK Bio and Tata's Advinus. He has authored more than 35 patents.

people.name: Parag Dilip Deshmukh
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Mumbai University with an MBA in human resources from IMT Ghaziabad. He has more than 24 years in active-ingredient manufacturing at Lupin, Aurobindo and Cipla, where he ran two plants. He joined Neuland in March 2025 to run its plants, focusing on efficiency and regulatory compliance.

companies.changes: Saharsh Davuluri took over as CEO & MD from his brother Sucheth in spring 2026 (announced early April); Sucheth became Executive Vice Chairman. No other executive departures found since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founder-run: the three co-founders from 2006 hold the top jobs. Ajay Bhardwaj is Chairman, MD & CEO; Dr. Ganesh Sambasivam (science) and K. C. Ravindra (operations) are whole-time directors. Ajay's son Ishaan is President. The four promoters and their families own about 71.4% (June 2026), down from 74.7% in March after promoter Aruna Ganesh sold 3.05%. True North has a nominee director.

people.name: Ajay Bhardwaj
people.relation: Co-founder; father of President Ishaan Bhardwaj
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in chemical engineering from IIT Delhi and a master's in chemical engineering from Louisiana State University. He started as a projects engineer at Max India and later was president of marketing and technical services at Biocon. He co-founded Anthem in 2006 with two Biocon/Syngene colleagues and has run it since, building a research-to-manufacturing contract business with unusually high margins. He has over 40 years in life sciences, contract research and drug manufacturing, was an EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2025 finalist, and is a founder and trustee of Plaksha University.

people.name: Ishaan Bhardwaj
people.relation: Son of the Chairman, MD & CEO Ajay Bhardwaj
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in engineering from Visvesvaraya Technological University (Belgaum) and a master's from George Washington University. He first worked at Anthem from January 2014 to December 2016, spent time at group company Anthem Cellutions, and rejoined in February 2019. He oversees purchasing, regulatory affairs, biological R&D, manufacturing and operations. He is a named promoter; he was Vice President at the 2025 listing and is now President.

people.name: Dr. Ganesh Sambasivam
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter (not related to the Bhardwajs)
people.bio: Has a BSc in chemistry from the University of Madras and an MSc in organic chemistry and a PhD in chemistry from the University of Pune. He spent more than a decade as Chief Scientific Officer of Syngene International before co-founding Anthem. He has over 30 years in process research and development and leads Anthem's science.

people.name: K. C. Ravindra (K Ravindra Chandrappa)
people.relation: Co-founder and promoter (not related to the Bhardwajs)
people.stake: 7.8% directly, plus about 2% through two family trusts he is trustee of (June 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Bangalore University. Before co-founding Anthem he worked at Cipla, Hikal and Biocon. He leads end-to-end operations: R&D, manufacturing, quality and regulatory compliance. He has more than 25 years in the pharma and biopharma industry, with a focus on running large plants to global quality standards.

people.name: Mohammed Gawir Baig
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from IIT Kharagpur with a postgraduate diploma in management from IIM Bangalore. He was a director at the investment bank O3 Capital, and earlier worked at Kea Healthcare and as a relationship manager at Standard Chartered Bank. He joined Anthem in November 2021 and led it through its July 2025 listing. Besides finance he handles planning, investor relations, ESG, HR, legal and compliance.

companies.changes: No executive changes found since the annual report. Promoter Aruna Ganesh sold her 3.05% in June 2026.

companies.styleNote: A father-and-son company: Dr. K. Ranga Raju, with the company since 1999, is executive Chairman, and his son Krishna Kanumuri is MD & CEO. The long-serving CFO, Siva Chittor, is a hired professional and also a whole-time director. The Kanumuri/Gokaraju promoter group owns about 34.5% (June 2026), mostly through family partnership firms; private-equity firm TPG is a large shareholder with a board nominee.

people.name: Krishna Kanumuri (Krishnam Raju Kanumuri)
people.since: Joined May 2004; re-appointed MD & CEO to Aug 2030
people.relation: Son of Chairman Dr. K. Ranga Raju
people.stake: 1.4% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together about 34.5%
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Manipal University with an MBA from the University of Kansas; he also attended the London School of Economics' 1995 summer school in financial markets. He worked at the telecom companies Sprint and Telmex before joining Sai in May 2004. As CEO he has built Sai into an integrated drug discovery, development and manufacturing partner for big pharma and biotech, including its dedicated-team model for large customers. He was re-appointed MD & CEO for five years from 1 September 2025.

people.name: Dr. K. Ranga Raju (Kanumuri Ranga Raju)
people.relation: Promoter; father of MD & CEO Krishna Kanumuri
people.stake: 0.1% directly; controls further shares as partner of two family firms, Sunflower Partners (7.4%) and Lily Partners (3.3%) (June 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in pharmacy from the University of Mysore, and bachelor's, master's and doctorate degrees in pharmacy from the Massachusetts College of Pharmacy, Boston. He has more than 40 years in the pharma industry and has been with Sai since it started in 1999, shaping its direction. He earlier sat on the board of Chemrich Fine Chemicals, a promoter-group company.

people.name: Sivaramakrishnan (Siva) Chittor
people.bio: A chartered accountant, cost accountant and qualified company secretary with more than 30 years of experience. He was administrative director and controller at IMRglobal (later CGI Information Systems & Management Consultants) and then senior vice president of shared services at Zavata. He joined Sai in January 2009 as senior vice president and head of finance, became CFO, and now also sits on the board as a whole-time director. His strengths are outsourcing, mergers and integration, restructuring and financial controls, and he was CFO through the December 2024 listing.

people.name: Dr. John Pavey
people.role: Senior Vice President & Head of Global Process R&D
people.bio: Holds a chemistry degree from the University of Oxford and a PhD in organic chemistry from the University of Liverpool, followed by postdoctoral research at the University of Cambridge. He has over 20 years in chemical development at Johnson & Johnson, UCB and AstraZeneca, taking active ingredients from discovery to commercial supply, including oligonucleotides, antibody-drug conjugates and peptides. He took over Sai's global process R&D on 1 April 2026 from the retiring Dr. Dean Edney.

companies.changes: Dr. John Pavey became head of global process R&D (senior management) on 1 Apr 2026, replacing Dr. Dean David Edney, who retired. No MD, CEO or CFO changes.

companies.styleNote: Run by its founders, the brothers Sanjeev Jain and Sandeep Jain, who are joint managing directors. A hired whole-time director runs operations and a hired CFO runs finance. The promoters own about 75.3% (June 2026): 17.2% each directly and 40.8% through the Akums Master Trust, of which the two brothers are trustees. Quadria Capital has a non-executive director.

people.name: Sanjeev Jain
people.relation: Co-founder; elder brother of Sandeep Jain
people.stake: 17.2% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also trustee of the Akums Master Trust (40.8%); family together about 75.3%
people.bio: Started in business in 1984 with his brother, running a small wholesale medicine shop in Old Delhi with ₹1.5 lakh from their father. In 1994 the brothers set up their first plant at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, and in 2004 they put their savings (and mortgaged their home) into a contract manufacturing plant in Haridwar, the start of Akums. He has about 40 years in pharma and handles the Delhi-side functions: purchasing, finance and marketing. He was named in Forbes India's DGEMS list in 2024 and received the India Pharma Leader award in 2018 and 2019.

people.name: Sandeep Jain
people.relation: Co-founder; younger brother of Sanjeev Jain
people.stake: 17.2% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also trustee of the Akums Master Trust (40.8%)
people.bio: Holds a BCom from Delhi University (1987). He co-founded the family's medicine trading business in 1984 and Akums in 2004. He lives in Haridwar and oversees manufacturing and operations across the company's 14 plants. He has an honorary doctorate from Apex University, Jaipur, and has received the IDMA Quality Excellence Award and a national award from the Government of India.

people.name: Sanjay Sinha
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in pharmaceutical sciences from Ranchi University and a master's in pharmacy from the University of Delhi. Before Akums he was President of Operations (Formulations) at Ipca Laboratories and President of Operations at Famy Care, Ahmedabad. At Akums he runs plant operations and sits on the board as a whole-time director.

people.name: Sumeet Sood
people.bio: A chartered accountant with about 30 years in accounts and finance. He worked at Arthur Andersen, Hindustan Times, Amar Ujala Publications and Jubilant Life Sciences, and was group CFO of Crystal before joining Akums as CFO in February 2022. He took the company through its August 2024 stock-market listing and presents the results on earnings calls.

companies.changes: No executive changes found since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Run by the founding brothers: Manoj Kumar Lohariwala is Chairman & Whole-time Director and Vinay Kumar Lohariwala is Managing Director. Both were re-appointed in May 2026 for another five years from March 2027. The promoters own about 50.9% (June 2026). A third founding partner of the original Innova partnership, Gian Parkash Aggarwal, is a large non-promoter shareholder.

people.name: Vinay Kumar Lohariwala
people.since: Founding partner (Innova partnership, 2006); MD, re-appointed to Mar 2032
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Chairman Manoj Kumar Lohariwala
people.bio: A mechanical engineer from Engineering College, Kota (University of Rajasthan). Before Innova he was vice-president, manufacturing at Pharmatech Health Care. In 2006 he co-founded the Innova Captab partnership with his brother and Gian Parkash Aggarwal; its business moved into the listed company in 2021. He has more than 20 years in making and marketing medicines and leads the company as MD.

people.name: Manoj Kumar Lohariwala
people.since: Founding partner (Innova partnership, 2006); re-appointed to Mar 2032
people.relation: Promoter; brother of MD Vinay Kumar Lohariwala
people.bio: Holds a BCom from Mohta College, Sadulpur (Maharshi Dayanand Saraswati University, Ajmer). Before Innova he was vice-president, marketing at Pharmatech Health Care. He co-founded the Innova Captab partnership in 2006 and has about 25–29 years in making and marketing medicines. He chairs the board as a whole-time (executive) director and is the largest individual shareholder.

people.name: Jayant Vasudeo Rao
people.bio: A chemistry graduate from the Arts, Science and Commerce College, Panvel (University of Bombay). He worked at Ebers Pharmaceuticals, Prophyla Biologicals and Lexicon Biotech, was production head at Scott-Edil Pharmacia and general manager (production and planning) at Brooks Laboratories. He has about 20 years in managing production of medicines and oversees manufacturing as a board member.

people.name: Lokesh Bhasin
people.bio: A cost and management accountant with a diploma in information systems security audit from the Institute of Cost Accountants of India. He has about 20 years in corporate finance and accounts. As deputy CFO he worked on the company's December 2023 listing from start to finish, and he was promoted to CFO on 30 March 2024 after the previous CFO, Gaurav Srivastava, resigned for personal reasons.

companies.changes: No executive departures found since the annual report. In May 2026 the board re-appointed both founder brothers for 2027–2032 (subject to the AGM vote).

companies.styleNote: The Bhartia family controls it, but a hired CEO & MD, Deepak Jain (ex-Bain), has run it since October 2023. Co-founder Hari S. Bhartia stays involved as executive Co-Chairman & Whole-time Director; his brother Shyam S. Bhartia is non-executive Chairman, and Shyam's son Priyavrat and Hari's daughter Aashti are non-executive directors. Promoters own about 45.2% (June 2026), mostly through family trustee companies.

people.name: Deepak Jain
people.bio: A chemical engineer from IIT Delhi (silver medallist) with an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad, where he was an industry scholar. He spent more than 18 years at Bain & Company, rising to senior partner leading its Asia-Pacific advanced manufacturing and services practice (autos, chemicals, cement), where he ran manufacturing and digital turnarounds and strategy programmes. He took over as CEO & MD on 1 October 2023 from Rajesh Kumar Srivastava. He is pushing the company towards specialty chemicals, nutrition and contract manufacturing.

people.name: Hari S. Bhartia
people.since: Co-founder of the Jubilant Bhartia Group
people.relation: Co-founder; brother of Chairman Shyam S. Bhartia; father of director Aashti Bhartia
people.stake: 0.2% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together about 45.2%
people.bio: A chemical engineer from IIT Delhi, which gave him its Distinguished Alumni award in 2000. With his brother Shyam he built the Jubilant Bhartia Group, which spans pharma, chemicals, food (Jubilant FoodWorks) and consumer businesses. He was President of the Confederation of Indian Industry in 2010–11 and has chaired the boards of IIM Raipur and IIT Kanpur. He is the only family member in an executive role at Ingrevia, and is also non-executive Co-Chairman of Jubilant Pharmova and Jubilant FoodWorks.

people.name: Vijay Kumar Srivastava
people.since: Joined Mar 2022; whole-time director since Nov 2024
people.bio: An IIT Kharagpur graduate with more than 25 years in manufacturing across petrochemicals, engineering polymers, agrochemicals and chemical intermediates. He began his career at UPL, spent many years at DuPont in India and abroad, and held leadership roles at Deepak Nitrite and SI Group. He joined Jubilant Ingrevia as President – Operations in March 2022 and joined the board as Chief of Operations & Whole-time Director on 1 November 2024 for five years.

people.name: Varun Gupta
people.bio: A chartered accountant (2005, all-India rank 43) who also completed an executive general management course at IIM Bangalore. After a short stint at Ernst & Young in risk advisory, he spent about 18 years at Unilever, starting as a management trainee at Hindustan Unilever and holding finance and commercial roles in India and abroad; his last job was head of finance for personal care, Unilever South Asia. He became CFO on 12 August 2024.

companies.changes: No executive changes since the annual report. During FY26 Arjun Shanker Bhartia left the board (Jul 2025) and his sister Aashti Bhartia joined as a non-executive director (Aug 2025).

companies.styleNote: Part of Arun Kumar (Pillai)'s Strides group, but run by hired managers. Arun Kumar, founder of Strides, is non-executive Chairman; CEO & MD Neeraj Sharma leads the business. The promoter group owns about 30.5% (June 2026), mostly through Tenshi Pharmaceuticals (18.4%) and Karuna Business Solutions (7.1%).

people.name: Neeraj Sharma
people.bio: An engineer in instrumentation and control from the University of Delhi with a postgraduate diploma in business management from IMT Ghaziabad. He has about 28–30 years in pharma across India, Southeast Asia, Latin America and Europe, including about 25 years at Ranbaxy and Sun Pharma, with a record in running P&Ls, entering new markets, turnarounds and acquisitions. He was CEO of Steriscience, the group's sterile-injectables business backed by TPG, before it was folded into OneSource. He now leads the combined CDMO covering biologics, drug-device combinations (such as GLP-1 cartridges) and soft gelatin capsules.

people.name: Anurag Bhagania
people.bio: A chartered accountant with an MBA in marketing and more than 25 years of experience, the last decade as CFO of listed companies. He worked at SKF, Honeywell and General Electric and was CFO of Kirloskar Oil Engines before joining OneSource.

people.name: Biju Mathew
people.bio: A pharmacist from Bangalore University with more than 28 years in quality systems and regulatory compliance. He was head of quality and a board member at Stelis Biopharma (the company's earlier name), and before that worked at Wockhardt Bio Pharma, Strides/Agila and Mylan. He has handled inspections by the US FDA, UK MHRA, Brazil's ANVISA and Australia's TGA, and has commissioned new plants.

people.name: Bernhard Thurnbauer
people.bio: Has more than 30 years in quality assurance, compliance and technical operations. He was global head of audit at Moderna and earlier worked at Roche, Acino and B. Braun. His expertise is sterile injectables, biologics and contract manufacturing under US FDA and European rules.

people.name: Jeffrey Wong
people.bio: Has more than 30 years in biopharma. He contributed to the Human Genome Project and held roles at Syngene, Fujifilm Diosynth, Thermo Fisher and Sartorius, covering bioprocessing, mammalian and microbial platforms and cell and gene therapy. At OneSource he leads partnerships and deal-making with global customers.

companies.changes: Senior VP (technical development) Prateek Gupta resigned effective 15 May 2026. Ravi Kumar, Global Head – Injectables and head of corporate strategy, resigned effective 24 Jul 2026; Preeti Kalra (HR head) was named senior management at the same time.

companies.styleNote: Part of the Gogri family's Aarti group (Aarti Industries, Aarti Drugs). From 1 Oct 2026 the Chairman, Rashesh C. Gogri, becomes Managing Director and his sister Hetal Gogri Gala moves from MD to Whole-time Director (staying Vice Chairperson); Narendra Salvi continues as the second MD. Their uncle Rajendra V. Gogri retired from the board at the Sep 2026 AGM. Chandrakant V. Gogri is Chairman Emeritus. The large promoter group owns about 42.9% (June 2026). About 45–48% of institutional votes went against the two role changes at the AGM.

people.name: Rashesh C. Gogri
people.since: On the board since Aug 2021; MD from Oct 2026
people.relation: Promoter; brother of Vice Chairperson Hetal Gogri Gala; nephew of former director Rajendra V. Gogri
people.stake: 4.2% (FY26 annual report, AGM notice); promoter group together about 42.9%
people.bio: A production engineer from Mumbai University, aged 52, with about 29 years in the chemical industry, where he helped grow several of the Aarti group's chemical and pharma businesses. He has been on the board since August 2021 and was non-executive Chairman before he takes over as Managing Director on 1 October 2026. He was Vice-Chairman & MD of Aarti Industries until 30 September 2026 and stays there as non-executive Vice-Chairman. He is also Managing Director of Aarti Drugs, so his time is split across group companies.

people.name: Hetal Gogri Gala
people.role: Vice Chairperson & Whole-time Director (MD until 30 Sep 2026)
people.since: On the board since Aug 2021; MD from Oct 2022
people.relation: Promoter; sister of Chairman Rashesh C. Gogri
people.bio: An electronics engineering graduate who also completed the Management Education Programme at IIM Ahmedabad and holds a degree in supply chain management. She has about 23 years in the chemical industry, with a focus on purchasing, supply chain, HR and administration. She was Managing Director from October 2022 and stepped down to Whole-time Director from 1 October 2026 to make way for her brother, while remaining Vice Chairperson. She is also a director of Aarti Industries.

people.name: Narendra J. Salvi
people.bio: Has more than three decades of experience in pharmaceuticals and specialty chemicals. As Managing Director he oversees operations, projects, regulatory compliance and sustainability. He has been on the board since the company was set up in 2021, and shareholders raised his salary ceiling in 2025 and granted him stock options under the company's 2023 option plan.

people.name: Piyush Lakhani
people.bio: The company's Chief Financial Officer and a key managerial person, who signs the financial statements. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

companies.changes: From 1 Oct 2026 Rashesh C. Gogri moves from non-executive Chairman to Managing Director and Hetal Gogri Gala from MD to Whole-time Director; approved at the 22 Sep 2026 AGM with heavy institutional opposition. Rajendra V. Gogri retired from the board at that AGM and was not replaced.

companies.styleNote: A Piramal family company: Nandini Piramal, daughter of group chairman Ajay Piramal, is Executive Chairperson, and her husband Peter DeYoung is an executive director and CEO of the global pharma business (CDMO and critical care). The CFO and business heads are hired professionals. Promoters own about 34.8% (June 2026), mostly through The Sri Krishna Trust (26.5%), whose trustees are Ajay and Swati Piramal.

people.name: Nandini Piramal
people.relation: Daughter of group chairman Ajay Piramal; wife of Executive Director Peter DeYoung
people.stake: 0.02% directly, plus 0.04% through the Nandini Piramal Trust (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together about 34.8%
people.bio: Holds a BA (Hons) in politics, philosophy and economics from Oxford and an MBA from Stanford Graduate School of Business, where she sits on the advisory council. As Chairperson she sets strategy across the company's 17 sites and oversees HR, finance, risk, IT and quality. She is a non-executive director of Piramal Enterprises and an adviser to the Piramal Foundation. Business Today named her among India's most powerful women in 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024, and she was a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2014. The board has proposed re-appointing her for three more years from April 2027.

people.name: Peter DeYoung
people.role: Executive Director & CEO, Piramal Global Pharma
people.since: Whole-time director since Oct 2023; re-appointment proposed from Oct 2026
people.relation: Husband of Chairperson Nandini Piramal; son-in-law of Ajay Piramal
people.bio: Holds a BS in engineering from Princeton (summa cum laude) and an MBA from Stanford (Arjay Miller Scholar). He worked at McKinsey in New York and Mumbai on pharma and healthcare, was seconded to the World Economic Forum's Global Health Initiative in Geneva, and then joined Blackstone's private-equity team in Mumbai. At Piramal he was President of Life Sciences and CEO of Piramal Critical Care before becoming CEO of Piramal Global Pharma, which covers the CDMO (Piramal Pharma Solutions) and critical-care businesses. The board has proposed a further three-year term from 6 October 2026.

people.name: Vivek Valsaraj
people.bio: A commerce graduate and associate member of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India, with more than 25 years in finance, over 21 of them in the Piramal group. Before Piramal he worked at Wockhardt and Bharat Bijlee. He runs finance and shared services, sits on the company's board as an executive director, and is a director of Allergan India and overseas subsidiaries. His areas are corporate finance, mergers, structuring, governance and tax.

people.name: Herve Berdou
people.role: Chief Operating Officer, Piramal Pharma Solutions
people.bio: Runs operations across the CDMO's drug-substance and drug-product sites, plus R&D, engineering, safety, project management, supply chain and IT. He was earlier VP, global operations and proposals, for cell and gene technologies at Lonza, and before that worked at Novartis and AstraZeneca-MedImmune. He has worked in Europe, the Middle East and the US.

people.name: Stuart Needleman
people.role: Chief Commercial Officer & Chief Patient Centricity Officer, Piramal Pharma Solutions
people.bio: A chemical engineer with an MBA, both from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, with nearly five decades in pharma services. He was President of Laurus Synthesis, President and COO of Aptuit, and held roles at Cambrex, Oxford Asymmetry, ChiRex and Rhodia Pharma Solutions. He leads global business development for the CDMO, from drug discovery and clinical development to commercial supply.

people.name: Jeffrey Hampton
people.role: President & Chief Operating Officer, Piramal Critical Care
people.bio: Holds a BS in marketing from the University of Florida and has more than 30 years in the industry. He was President of Accord Healthcare and worked at Apotex, Osmotica, Dabur and IVAX/Teva. He runs the hospital-generics business (anaesthesia gases, pain and injectables), including operations, regulatory affairs, sales and product development.

companies.changes: No CEO or CFO changes. Company Secretary Tanya Sanish left in Feb 2026; Maneesh Sharma became Company Secretary from 29 Apr 2026. The FY26 AGM notice proposes re-appointing Peter DeYoung (from Oct 2026) and Nandini Piramal (from Apr 2027) for three years each.

companies.styleNote: A Bhartia family company run by the next generation: Priyavrat Bhartia (son of Chairman Shyam S. Bhartia) is MD and Arjun Shanker Bhartia (son of Co-Chairman Hari S. Bhartia) is Joint MD, both since June 2023. The founder brothers Shyam (Chairman) and Hari (Co-Chairman) are now non-executive promoter directors. Hired CEOs run the businesses, including Chris Preti at the US sterile-injectables CDMO. Promoters own about 47.7% (June 2026), mostly through family trustee companies.

people.name: Priyavrat Bhartia
people.since: MD since Jun 2023; on the board since May 2017
people.relation: Son of Chairman Shyam S. Bhartia; cousin of Joint MD Arjun Shanker Bhartia
people.stake: 0.9% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together about 47.7%
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in economics from Dartmouth College and an MBA from Stanford. He has about 26–29 years of industry experience, and joined the Jubilant Pharmova board as a non-executive director in May 2017. He became MD in June 2023, when his uncle Hari S. Bhartia stepped back, as part of a planned handover to the next generation. He also sits on the boards of Jubilant Ingrevia, Jubilant Industries and the family's media companies, including HT Media and Hindustan Media Ventures. Shareholders approved his continuation as MD by postal ballot in August 2026.

people.name: Arjun Shanker Bhartia
people.since: Joint MD since Jun 2023; on the board since May 2017
people.relation: Son of Co-Chairman Hari S. Bhartia; cousin of MD Priyavrat Bhartia
people.bio: A graduate of Brown University (2008) who began his career as an associate consultant at Bain & Company (2008–2010). He has about 18–19 years of industry experience and joined the board as a non-executive director in May 2017. He became Joint MD in June 2023 and is responsible for the overall management of the company under the board. He is also a director of family companies Jubilant Beverages, Jubilant Consumer and Jubilant Enpro. He was paid ₹75m in FY26, and shareholders approved his continuation in August 2026.

people.name: Ashish Mukkirwar
people.bio: Holds an MBA from IIM Calcutta and has over 20 years in corporate finance, capital markets, investor relations, mergers and strategy. He was Group Vice President & CFO of the global formulations business at Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, and earlier held senior roles in investment banking at Moelis & Company and UBS. He became CFO on 23 May 2026.

people.name: Chris Preti
people.since: President of Jubilant HollisterStier from Mar 2023
people.bio: Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in chemistry from Furman University, an MBA in international business from the University of South Carolina, and completed an executive leadership programme at Wharton. He spent about 25 years at GSK and HollisterStier Allergy in R&D, sales and marketing and operations, and was President of HollisterStier Allergy before taking over the contract manufacturing business in 2023. He leads the sterile fill-finish sites at Spokane and Montreal, including the $285m expansion with a third line and a fourth under construction. He was named a 2026 Person of Influence by the Spokane Journal of Business.

companies.changes: CFO Arun Kumar Sharma stepped down on 22 May 2026 to become adviser to the Chairmen; Ashish Mukkirwar took over on 23 May 2026. Earlier, in FY26, Group CFO and whole-time director Arvind Chokhany resigned (Sep 2025) and whole-time director Dr. Ramakrishnan Arul left the board (Aug 2025). Shareholders re-approved the MD and Joint MD in Aug 2026.

companies.styleNote: Promoter Swapnil Shah is Managing Director and runs the company; co-promoter Ashokkumar Barot is a non-executive director. Two whole-time directors handle finance and operations. The chairman, chartered accountant Sanjay Majmudar, is non-executive. The annual report says no directors are related to each other. Promoters own about 45.8% (June 2026), spread across Swapnil Shah (7.7%), Ashokkumar Barot (7.5%), listed Remus Pharmaceuticals (7.1%) and other group entities and relatives.

people.name: Swapnil Jatinbhai Shah
people.relation: Promoter
people.stake: 7.7% (June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together about 45.8%
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Nirma University with an MBA from Hofstra University, New York. He has more than 18 years in pharma and earlier ran operations at a specialty pharma distribution company. As MD since October 2021 he leads the product portfolio, strategy and business development, and sits on the board of the US subsidiary Havix (Aavis Pharmaceuticals). He is also non-executive Chairman of Remus Pharmaceuticals, a listed promoter-group company, and convenor of the pharma panel of CII's Gujarat council. In 2025 shareholders were asked to raise his pay to ₹7.5 crore a year.

people.name: Deval Rajnikant Shah
people.bio: Has been on the board since January 2020 and serves as whole-time director and CFO, signing the company's accounts. He was paid about ₹1.1 crore in FY26. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

people.name: Chetan Bipinchandra Shah
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from Lukhdhirji Engineering College (Saurashtra University) and a postgraduate diploma in industrial engineering from NITIE, plus diplomas in industrial management, HR development and labour laws. He has more than three decades of experience, over 25 years in pharma at Torrent Pharmaceuticals and Cadila Pharmaceuticals, and also worked at Reliance Retail, Reliance Fresh and Reliance Corporate IT Park. He joined the board in November 2023 as whole-time director and COO and runs end-to-end operations, supply chain, manufacturing, MIS and HR.

companies.changes: No executive changes found since the annual report. Independent director Dr. Viranchi Shah joins the board from 26 Aug 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Desai family company founded in 2013: founder Ashwin Desai is MD, his wife Purnima and sons Rohan and Dr. Aman are whole-time directors. The non-executive Chairman, Kamalvijay Tulsian, is Rohan's father-in-law, and non-executive director Ishita Manjrekar is Aman's wife. Promoters own about 74.9% (June 2026), including four Desai family trusts holding about 50.6%.

people.name: Ashwin Jayantilal Desai
people.relation: Founder; husband of Purnima Desai; father of Rohan and Dr. Aman Desai
people.stake: 5.1% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also a trustee of four family trusts (about 50.6%); family together about 74.9%
people.bio: A chemical engineer from the Institute of Chemical Technology (ICT), Mumbai (1974), which gave him its Distinguished Alumnus award in 2010. He was a founding member of Anupam Rasayan India and its Chairman & MD until 2013, when he left to set up Aether. As MD he sets the company's overall direction and leads techno-commercial work, R&D and its continuous-flow chemistry capability.

people.name: Purnima Ashwin Desai
people.relation: Wife of MD Ashwin Desai; mother of Rohan and Dr. Aman Desai
people.stake: 17.4% directly (June 2026 shareholding pattern); also a trustee of the family trusts
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Delhi (1975) and has decades of experience in specialty chemicals. She was a director of Anupam Rasayan India until 2013. At Aether she oversees accounting and finance.

people.name: Rohan Ashwin Desai
people.relation: Son of Ashwin and Purnima Desai; brother of Dr. Aman Desai; son-in-law of Chairman Kamalvijay Tulsian
people.bio: A commerce graduate from SPB (VNSG University), Surat, with long experience in specialty chemicals. He was a director of Anupam Rasayan India until 2013. At Aether he runs the commercial side: sales, finance, strategic procurement, HR and systems.

people.name: Dr. Aman Ashwinbhai Desai
people.relation: Son of Ashwin and Purnima Desai; brother of Rohan Desai; husband of director Ishita Manjrekar
people.bio: Holds a bachelor's in chemical technology from ICT Mumbai (2005) and a PhD in organic chemistry (chiral chemistry) from Michigan State University (2010). He was a project leader in process development at Dow Chemical in Michigan before joining the family business. He leads R&D, the pilot plant, production, new projects and technical business development, the core of Aether's contract research and manufacturing work. He has co-authored 25 international papers and four US patents and won ICT's Young Achiever Award in 2018.

people.name: Dr. James (Jim) W. Ringer
people.bio: Holds a BS in chemistry from Purdue and a PhD in organic chemistry from the University of Wisconsin. He spent 30 years in R&D at Dow Chemical (1988–2018), including as director of process chemistry, and later worked with Corteva AgriScience. He is co-inventor on 22 US patents and became Aether's CTO on 1 March 2024.

people.name: Faiz A. Nagariya
people.bio: The company's Chief Financial Officer and a key managerial person, who co-signs the CEO/CFO certificate in the annual report. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

companies.changes: No executive or senior-management changes during FY26 or since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Controlled by private-equity firm Advent International, which owns 57.5% through two holding companies (Behryanda 33.3%, Jusmirial 24.2%) and has pledged 94.6% of it; Advent partners sit on the board as non-executive directors. There is no founding family in management. The company is run by hired professionals under Umang Vohra, ex-Cipla CEO, who became Chairman in May 2026 and Group CEO later that month. The top team has turned over almost completely in the past 15 months.

people.name: Umang Vohra
people.since: Chairman from 1 May 2026; Group CEO from 20 May 2026
people.bio: An engineering graduate from M.S. Ramaiah Institute of Technology with an MBA from T.A. Pai Management Institute. He has over 30 years in pharma and healthcare, with leadership roles at PepsiCo India, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories and Cipla. As Managing Director and Global CEO of Cipla he led growth in respiratory, speciality, digital health and manufacturing. He joined Cohance as Chairman on 1 May 2026, became Group CEO on 20 May 2026, and shareholders approved his appointment in June 2026. He took over during a sharp downturn: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 23% and the $1bn FY30 target is now called an aspiration.

people.name: Yann D'Herve
people.bio: Holds a master's in chemistry from CPE Lyon and an MBA from Université de Picardie Jules Verne. He has over 30 years in pharma, healthcare, speciality chemicals and CDMO. Before Cohance he was Senior Vice President and General Manager of Evonik's healthcare business line, running 2,600 people across nine plants with full profit responsibility, and earlier held sales, services and speciality-ingredients roles at Evonik. He runs the pharma CDMO business, which is the company's core.

people.name: Gunjan Singh
people.bio: An alumnus of IIT Delhi and SP Jain Institute of Management and Research, Mumbai. He began as a strategy consultant at Accenture and later held leadership roles at Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Wanbury, Jubilant Pharmova and Piramal Pharma. With over two decades across active ingredients, formulations and CDMO services, he runs Cohance's API+ business.

people.name: Amrit Singh
people.bio: A chemical engineer with an executive MBA and more than two decades at Navin Fluorine, SRF, UPL and Unilever. His previous job was CEO of Navin Fluorine's speciality chemicals business unit, where he grew the business through capacity additions and customer partnerships. He now leads Cohance's speciality chemicals platform.

people.name: Ravinatha Shetty
people.bio: A chemical engineer with a strategic-management qualification from IIM Kozhikode and nearly 35 years at Lupin, Watson Pharma, Zydus Cadila, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's and Aurobindo Pharma. He oversees supply chain, safety and environment, operational excellence and corporate affairs across the company's sites.

people.name: Sunilkumar Singh
people.bio: Has over 35 years in quality across active ingredients, formulations and CDMO plants. He was global head of quality for Dr. Reddy's PSAI business and global head of internal audit and compliance there, and earlier held roles at Mylan, Zydus, Glenmark and Cipla. His job matters now: the company has a US FDA warning letter at Nacharam and FDA observations at three more sites since July.

companies.changes: CFO and whole-time director Himanshu Agarwal resigned in June 2026 and left on 13 Sep 2026; no successor named yet. Executive Chairman Vivek Sharma left on 30 Apr 2026 and Umang Vohra replaced him (Chairman 1 May, Group CEO 20 May 2026). Earlier in FY26, CEO Dr. Sudhir Kumar Singh resigned (Jul 2025) and MD Dr. V. Prasada Raju resigned (Oct 2025). A new Company Secretary, Sisir K. Mishra, joined in Apr 2026.

companies.styleNote: A Vyas family company. Founder Janmejay R. Vyas died in May 2025; his son Arpit Vyas is Global Managing Director and his widow Deohooti Vyas is a whole-time director. Aditi Vyas and Mansi Vyas, both in the promoter group, are in senior management. The Swiss arm Carbogen Amcis is run by a hired CEO, Stephan Fritschi. Promoters own 59.3% (June 2026), all through Adimans Technologies LLP, in which Deohooti has an 80% profit share and Arpit 20%. The promoter plans to lend the company up to CHF 200m, backed largely by personal assets, to repay costly Indian debt.

people.name: Arpit J. Vyas
people.since: On the board since 2012; MD since 2017 (of predecessor DPCL from 2014)
people.relation: Son of late founder Janmejay R. Vyas and Whole-time Director Deohooti J. Vyas
people.stake: Under 0.01% directly (1,000 shares, FY26 annual report); 20% profit share in Adimans Technologies LLP, which owns 59.3%
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Aston University, Birmingham, aged 40. He joined the board of the predecessor company Dishman Pharmaceuticals and Chemicals as a whole-time director in June 2009, became its MD in June 2014 and also CFO in July 2015. After the 2017 merger he became MD & CFO of Dishman Carbogen Amcis, then Global Managing Director, giving up the CFO role in November 2018. He is in charge of strategy, marketing and sales, finance, legal and IT across the group's plants in India, Switzerland, France and elsewhere. He took no salary from the Indian company in FY26 but was paid as a director of a foreign subsidiary.

people.name: Deohooti J. Vyas
people.since: Re-appointed for five years from Sep 2026
people.relation: Widow of founder Janmejay R. Vyas; mother of Global MD Arpit J. Vyas
people.stake: 80% profit share in Adimans Technologies LLP, which owns 59.3% (FY26 annual report; June 2026 shareholding pattern)
people.bio: A promoter and whole-time director of the company, and a partner with an 80% profit share in Adimans Technologies LLP, the holding LLP through which the family owns the company. The board re-appointed her as a whole-time director for five years from 3 September 2026, approved by shareholders in September 2025. Her education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

people.name: Harshil R. Dalal
people.role: Global Chief Financial Officer (also Deputy CEO, Carbogen Amcis)
people.bio: The group's Global CFO and a key managerial person; at Carbogen Amcis he is also Deputy CEO and sits on its board. He drew his FY26 pay from a foreign subsidiary rather than the Indian company. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

people.name: Dr. Stephan Fritschi
people.bio: Heads Carbogen Amcis, the group's Swiss-based contract development and manufacturing arm, and sits on its board. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

people.name: Paolo Armanino
people.bio: Named as Chief Operating Officer for India and senior management in the FY26 annual report, responsible for the Indian plants. His education and earlier career are not given in the sources reviewed.

companies.changes: Founder and Chairman Janmejay R. Vyas died on 27 May 2025. No executive departures found since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founder Manish Grover is Managing Director and also chairs the board. His wife Bhavna Grover and daughter Shreya Grover are whole-time directors. Manish Grover alone owns about 63% and the promoter group 63.6% (June 2026). Two outside executives joined the board in July 2026.

people.name: Manish Grover
people.since: Founded Shuddhi Ayurveda in 2009; MD since Aug 2021; re-appointed to Aug 2031
people.relation: Founder; husband of Bhavna Grover and father of Shreya Grover
people.stake: 63.27% (7.86 crore shares, June 2026 shareholding pattern); promoter group together 63.62%
people.bio: He holds a B.Com from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut. He began promoting Ayurveda as an entrepreneur in 2009, founding the Shuddhi Ayurveda brand, and set up Jeena Sikho Lifecare in 2017. He is the public face of the Shuddhi brand on television and digital platforms, and built the HIIMS hospital chain and the medicines business. The board re-appointed him as MD for five years from 25 August 2026, with pay of up to ₹6 crore a year (up from ₹2.4 crore), subject to shareholder approval. He also sits on several group and private companies, including Shuddhi Lifecare, Jeena Green Resources and an AIF manager, CSAIPL AIF Fund Management.

people.name: Bhavna Grover
people.since: Director since incorporation (2017); whole-time director since Aug 2021
people.relation: Co-promoter; wife of Manish Grover and mother of Shreya Grover
people.bio: She is an arts graduate from Punjab University. The company says she has over seven years of experience in human resources, legal administration and organisational management, and has been with the company since it was set up. She oversees governance, compliance and internal systems. The board proposed re-appointing her from 25 August 2026 at pay of up to ₹1.8 crore a year.

people.name: Shreya Grover
people.since: Board member earlier as non-executive; whole-time director since 27 Aug 2025
people.relation: Daughter of Manish and Bhavna Grover
people.bio: The company presents her as the next generation of the family. She works on branding, sales, marketing and business development for its Ayurvedic and wellness products. She was moved from a non-executive seat to whole-time director in August 2025. The annual report does not give her education or earlier jobs.

people.name: Ankush Kaushal
people.bio: He holds a B.Sc. in hotel and hospitality management. The company credits him with over 26 years in hospitality, healthcare, wellness and business transformation, including senior roles with Indian and international hospitality and healthcare groups, which it does not name. He works on hospital operations, wellness expansion and strategy. His two-year term runs to July 2028 at pay of about ₹65 lakh a year.

people.name: Dr. Ish Sharma
people.bio: He holds BAMS, MD and PhD degrees in Ayurveda and an MBA in human resource management, and has over 20 years in Ayurveda teaching, research, hospital administration and clinical practice. He was Academic Chair in Ayurveda Medicine at the University of Mauritius, Controller of Examinations at Guru Ravidas Ayurved University, Punjab, and Principal of Babeke Ayurveda Medical College, Punjab. He has written books and research papers. At Jeena Sikho he leads the medical and research side, on a two-year term to July 2028.

people.name: Nanak Chand
people.since: CFO through FY26 (start date not disclosed)
people.bio: He holds a B.Com (Hons) and is a CMA (Executive level). He has over 15 years of experience in financial management, planning and business development, including cost accounting, internal audit, corporate restructuring and equity research. He runs the company's finance function, statutory compliance and ERP work.

people.name: Sahil Jain
people.since: COO since 27 Aug 2025; with the company about 8 years
people.relation: Listed in the promoter group (the filings do not say how he is related)
people.bio: He holds a B.Com and a Master of Computer Applications, and earlier worked with IBM and HCL Australia. In about eight years at Jeena Sikho he has run IT, marketing, the call centre and administration. As COO he oversees operations across the business.

companies.changes: Company Secretary Smita Chaturvedi resigned on 14 Jul 2026; Priya Goyal replaced her. Ankush Kaushal and Dr. Ish Sharma joined as whole-time directors on 15 Jul 2026. The earlier auditor, KRA & Co, resigned in Aug 2025.

companies.styleNote: Founder Vasant Rathi, who lives in the US, is non-executive chairman; he owns 26.7% himself and the promoter group 43.2% (June 2026). His daughter Rasika Rathi is a non-executive director and also general counsel of the US subsidiary. Day-to-day, the only executive director is long-serving Mukund Kabra, who is not classed as a promoter. OrbiMed owns 12.1%.

people.name: Mukund Kabra
people.since: Joined 1995; on the board since Sep 1999; re-appointment to Mar 2032 proposed
people.bio: A chemical engineer from Sambalpur University with about 31 years in the enzyme industry, all of them at this company. He oversees manufacturing and fermentation work: improving strains, downstream processing and analytical research. He also sits on the boards of several subsidiaries. The board has proposed another five-year term from April 2027; his FY26 pay was ₹2.87 crore. His daughter Manasi Kabra works at the US subsidiary.

people.name: Beni Prasad Rauka
people.since: CFO since 2002 (joined as a consultant in 2000)
people.bio: A chartered accountant and company secretary. He joined Advanced Enzymes in 2000 as a consultant, became CFO in 2002, and since 2007 has run finance for the whole group as it added subsidiaries. He is also a director of group companies including Advanced Bio-Agro Tech, Advanced Enzytech Solutions and JC Biotech.

people.name: Harshad Doshi
people.bio: The annual report names him as CFO and COO of the US subsidiaries, which carry most of the group's goodwill. It gives no further biography.

companies.changes: Senior VP (marketing and business development) Dipak Roda left on 9 Apr 2026. Independent director Rajshree Patel's term ended on 11 Jun 2026; Pradip Shah, a US-based entrepreneur and board member from 1993 to 2016, joined as an independent director.

companies.styleNote: Run by the Kelkar family. Brothers Vikram Kelkar (MD) and Dr. Nikhil Kelkar (Joint MD) lead the business. Their father, founder Arun Kelkar, left the board as Chairman on 28 Sep 2026 but still owns 18.6%. The family owns 64.3% (June 2026). An operations manager, Raghunath Sawant, joined the board in Aug 2026.

people.name: Vikram Kelkar
people.relation: Son of founder Arun Kelkar; brother of Dr. Nikhil Kelkar
people.bio: He holds a bachelor's in management studies from the University of Mumbai and a master's in international business from the University of Auckland. He has over 20 years in the food and nutrition business and runs the premix and therapeutic food (RUF/MNP) businesses in India and abroad. He won a Young Visionary award in 2011 for innovation in fighting micronutrient deficiency, and co-wrote a 2011 research paper on wheat flour fortification. Shareholders were asked to approve pay of up to ₹2.42 crore a year from April 2026.

people.name: Dr. Nikhil Kelkar
people.relation: Son of founder Arun Kelkar; brother of Vikram Kelkar
people.bio: He holds a dental surgery degree from Nair Hospital Dental College (University of Mumbai) and a diploma in marketing management from NMIMS. He practised as a dental surgeon for seven years and was a member of the New Zealand Dental Association; he is a New Zealand national. He has over 15 years in the food and nutrition business, heads the branded nutrition products business in India and abroad, and runs group finance. Shareholders re-appointed him at the September 2026 AGM.

people.name: Raghunath Sawant
people.role: Executive Director (also GM, Operations and Corporate Quality)
people.since: Joined Jul 2022; Executive Director from 12 Aug 2026
people.bio: He holds a diploma in food technology from the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education. He has over 17 years in quality assurance, regulatory work and operations, previously at Chitale Sweets and Snacks, Godrej and Boyce and Parle Agro. He joined Hexagon in July 2022 as General Manager, Operations and Corporate Quality. Shareholders approved his five-year board term in September 2026, at pay of up to ₹50.6 lakh a year.

people.name: Soman Nemai Jana
people.since: CFO at the time of the 2026 IPO (start date not disclosed)
people.bio: A chartered accountant who rose inside Hexagon through roles including General Manager, Accounts and Finance, and DGM, Corporate Finance, before becoming CFO. Earlier he headed the accounts and tax department at Jatin Shah and Associates and trained with Agharkar and Company. He was CFO through the June 2026 listing.

companies.changes: Founder Arun Kelkar left as Chairman and Executive Director on 28 Sep 2026 at the end of his term. The board had proposed re-appointing him, but the AGM results filing lists only the approvals for Nikhil Kelkar and Raghunath Sawant. Executive Director Subhash Kelkar (Arun's brother) and non-executive director Aditya Kelkar resigned on 6 Jul 2026 after selling shares in the IPO.

companies.styleNote: Four promoter directors, all named Patel, run the company as executives, and there is no outside CEO or CFO: the MD doubles as CFO. The annual report does not say whether the four are related to each other. Together with relatives, promoters own 53.0% (June 2026).

people.name: Vasant Vadilal Patel
people.since: Promoter and first director since incorporation; re-appointed to May 2029
people.relation: Promoter
people.bio: He holds a diploma in chemical engineering and has over 21 years in dyes, intermediates, pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals. Before founding Accent Microcell he worked at a pharmaceutical and laboratory chemicals company. He runs export marketing, product development and policy. His term was renewed for three years from May 2026.

people.name: Ghanshyam Arjanbhai Patel
people.role: Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer
people.since: Promoter and founder; re-appointed as MD to May 2029
people.relation: Promoter
people.bio: A commerce graduate with over 20 years in finance, accounts, tax and management, and in marketing agro products, rice processing and excipients. He leads strategy, administration, finance, HR and banking, and also serves as the company's CFO. The company credits him with making funding cheaper and tightening finance. His term was renewed for three years from May 2026.

people.name: Nitin Jasvantbhai Patel
people.since: Promoter and director since inception; re-appointed to May 2029
people.relation: Promoter
people.bio: A commerce graduate with over 20 years in pharma as a technical director. He runs plant projects from planning to completion, meets production and quality targets, and leads R&D. The company cites his experience building greenfield plants, which matters for the delayed Unit III.

people.name: Vinodbhai Manibhai Patel
people.relation: Promoter
people.bio: An arts graduate who started on the shop floor. He has 20–25 years in pharmaceutical excipients and helped launch the business's operations across India in 2002. He built and ran the first plant at Pirana, handles industrial relations and leads CSR work.

companies.changes: Independent director Chintan Bhatt resigned on 29 Jun 2026; Pooja Shah joined as an independent director on 6 Jul 2026.

companies.styleNote: Carlyle controls the company through CA Harbor and CA Hull Investments, which own 61.3% (June 2026) and sit on the board only as non-executive directors. Since the Viyash merger in December 2025, the company is run by hired managers led by Viyash founder-CEO Dr. Haribabu Bodepudi. The chairman, Dr. Kamal Sharma, is independent. No directors are related to each other.

people.name: Dr. Haribabu Bodepudi
people.since: On the board since Aug 2023; MD & Group CEO since 16 Dec 2025 (term to Dec 2027)
people.stake: 2.77% (1.21 crore shares) plus 2.03 crore convertible warrants (March 2026)
people.bio: He holds a PhD in organic chemistry from Andhra University and has over 30 years in API and tablet research, manufacturing, quality and operations. At Mylan over about 20 years he was COO and then CEO of Mylan India and later Mylan's global COO, responsible for more than 50 plants. He led Mylan's move into HIV (ARV) drugs and grew that business past $800 million with over half the market. He then led Carlyle-backed Viyash Life Sciences, which merged into Sequent, and now runs the combined group.

people.name: Rajaram Narayanan
people.role: Whole-time Director and CEO, Animal Health
people.since: On the board since Apr 2022 (then MD & CEO); current role since 16 Dec 2025
people.bio: He holds a BE (Hons) in electrical and electronics from BITS Pilani and an MBA from IIFT, New Delhi, and completed Harvard Business School's Advanced Management Program. He spent over 18 years at Hindustan Unilever in India and Asia, was Chief Marketing Officer at Airtel, and was MD and Country Chair of Sanofi India before joining Sequent. He was Sequent's MD and CEO until the merger, and now runs the animal-health business. His term runs to April 2027.

people.name: Srinivas Vasireddy
people.role: Whole-time Director (SVP and Head, API Operations)
people.bio: He has about 37 years in API operations, covering manufacturing, production planning, third-party manufacturing, quality, compliance and safety. He was head of API special projects at Mylan, then ran API operations across all Viyash units before the merger. He now heads API operations for the combined company.

people.name: Ramakant Singani
people.bio: He has 31 years in finance, including business finance, accounting, planning and analysis, ERP projects and cost management. Before Viyash he was head of finance for global manufacturing operations at Dr. Reddy's. He joined Viyash as CFO in September 2021 and took over as CFO of the merged listed company in January 2026.

companies.changes: Previous CFO Saurav Bhala resigned from 1 Jan 2026. Whole-time director Vedprakash Ragate resigned on 30 Sep 2025. Senior manager Ashish Kakabalia left in Dec 2025. AVP Legal Phillip Trott died in May 2026. The company was renamed Viyash Scientific in Jan 2026.

companies.styleNote: Founder Sujit Bhayani is Chairman and MD, and Shanil Bhayani, who the annual report says is related to him, is a whole-time director. Promoters own 76.2% (June 2026): 40.4% through Riva Resources and the rest held by Sujit, his HUF, Avani and Shanil Bhayani. The only non-family executives are a hired operations director and CFO. Milin Mehta, a chartered accountant, joined in June 2026 as a non-executive (not independent) director.

people.name: Sujit Jaysukh Bhayani
people.relation: Founder and promoter; related to Shanil Bhayani (per annual report)
people.stake: 21.16% directly plus 5.72% through his HUF (June 2026); promoter group together 76.15%, including 40.35% through Riva Resources
people.bio: He is a chemistry graduate from the University of Tulsa, USA, with over 35 years running the company. In 1989 it started with one plant making two calcium products; he has built it into a maker of mineral-based excipients and nutrition ingredients with subsidiaries in Europe and the US, plus a battery-materials unit. He sets long-term strategy and leads innovation and diversification, including the new battery-materials business (Sudeep Advanced Materials). He took the company public in November 2025.

people.name: Shanil Sujit Bhayani
people.relation: Promoter; related to Chairman & MD Sujit Bhayani (per annual report)
people.bio: He is a finance graduate from Drexel University, USA, with over nine years in sales and marketing planning, product development and running staff. He introduces new products for pharma customers and leads the push into nutrition ingredients through Sudeep Nutrition. He also co-signs the Board's report with the MD.

people.name: Ajay Shrirang Kandelkar
people.since: Joined Oct 2023 as VP Operations; whole-time director since 13 Sep 2024 (term to Sep 2029)
people.bio: He holds a bachelor's in dairy technology from Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth. Before Sudeep he worked at Food Service (India), Drytech Processes (India), the Warana dairy cooperative (Shree Warana Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Prakriya Sangh) and Taiyo Lucid. He runs production, engineering, quality and stores across the company's plants. Shareholders were asked to approve a pay rise from April 2026.

people.name: Ketan Vyas
people.bio: A chartered accountant with an MBA in finance from the University of Mumbai and 26 years in finance. He previously worked at Neogen Chemicals, ArcelorMittal and Batliboi. He became CFO in September 2024, ahead of the November 2025 IPO.

people.name: Serkan Celebi
people.bio: He runs business development, strategy and planning for the European subsidiary. He has 14 years of business experience and previously worked at Van Eeghen & Co. in the Netherlands.

people.name: Sendhil Kumar Pani
people.role: Managing Director, Sudeep Pharma USA Inc.
people.bio: He oversees strategy, finances and operations of the US subsidiary. He previously worked at IMCD US and at US Nutraceuticals (Valensa International).

companies.changes: Milin Mehta, managing partner of K C Mehta & Co, joined as a non-executive director on 26 Jun 2026. The investor nominee director, Pranav Parikh, resigned in Jun 2025.

companies.styleNote: Founder Saurabh Garg is Chairman and MD and owns 43.7% after the May 2026 IPO. His wife Amita Garg (16.9%) and son Ayush Garg sit on the board as non-executive promoter directors, though the company says Ayush leads finance, technology and planning, and he draws a salary. Promoters own 67.5% (May 2026). Most sales go to POCT Services, a partnership in which a director is a partner.

people.name: Saurabh Garg
people.since: Founder; with the company since incorporation (2010)
people.relation: Founder and promoter; husband of director Amita Garg and father of director Ayush Garg
people.stake: 43.69% (May 2026, after IPO; 62.62% before it); promoter group together 67.51%
people.bio: He holds a diploma in electronics engineering from Lucknow Polytechnic and has over 31 years in healthcare and diagnostics. He built the business around turnkey diagnostic laboratories and critical-care and cardiology solutions, working closely with government health programmes. He leads business development and strategy. He has received the Jan Swasthya Sewa Award (2018) and a Pride of Asia award for healthcare innovation.

people.name: Yethadka Subraya Prabhakara
people.bio: He holds a B.Sc. in agricultural marketing and co-operation and an M.Sc. in agricultural economics from the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore, and a postgraduate diploma in agricultural management from IIM Ahmedabad. He has about 31 years in general management and running profit-and-loss units. The company says he is responsible for its overall strategy and operations.

people.name: Ajay Kumar Mahanty
people.relation: Promoter (not stated to be related to the Gargs)
people.bio: He holds an MBA from Berhampur University and an honours diploma for a B.Sc. from Utkal University. He has over 20 years in sales, marketing and strategy in diagnostics. He leads sales and marketing planning, oversees manufacturing and budgeting, drives partnerships and heads R&D to widen the product range.

people.name: Kuldeep Chowdhry
people.bio: He holds an MBA from Sikkim Manipal University and a B.Sc. from Kanpur University, and completed XLRI's executive programme in strategy and leadership. He has over 29 years in biotechnology. He oversees operations, coordinating R&D, production and quality control, and new product development.

people.name: Meenal Gupta
people.since: CFO through FY26 (start date not disclosed)
people.bio: She is CFO and signs the MD/CFO certification with Saurabh Garg. The annual report gives no education or career details; her FY26 pay was about ₹48 lakh.

companies.changes: Listed on NSE SME in May 2026. Prabhakara joined the board as a whole-time director in May 2025, ahead of the IPO. No executive resignations have been filed since the annual report.

companies.styleNote: Founder Rajiv Gandhi is CEO and MD, and his daughter Priya Gandhi is Executive Director. His uncle, Dr. Bhupendra Gandhi, is non-executive chairman and his brother Sanjiv Gandhi is a non-executive director. The Gandhi family and group firms own 53.7% (June 2026). Ravin and Bela Gandhi, who live abroad, are being moved out of the promoter group.

people.name: Rajiv Gandhi
people.since: Founder (1987); re-appointed for 3 years from 1 Apr 2026
people.relation: Founder; father of Priya Gandhi, brother of Sanjiv Gandhi, nephew of Chairman Dr. Bhupendra Gandhi
people.stake: 10.48% (June 2026); his wife Nina Gandhi 8.19%; promoter group together 53.73%
people.bio: He is a graduate of Bombay University and founded Hester in 1987. He manages the whole company, with all functional heads reporting to him, and built its poultry and livestock vaccine business in India, Nepal and Tanzania. He won the Ahmedabad Management Association's Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2016, is president of the AMA and a past chairman of FICCI's Gujarat State Council. He sits on the governing councils of SVNIT Surat and Kamdhenu University. His pay from April 2026 is ₹18 lakh a month before other benefits.

people.name: Priya Gandhi
people.since: With the company since 2016; re-appointed from 28 Oct 2026 to Mar 2029
people.relation: Daughter of CEO & MD Rajiv Gandhi; niece of Sanjiv Gandhi
people.bio: She has an undergraduate degree from the Srishti School of Art, Design and Technology, Bengaluru, and a postgraduate degree in management for family business from ISB Hyderabad. She joined Hester in 2016 and works on strategy, organisation building and coordination across businesses and subsidiaries. Her focus includes operations, business expansion, corporate communications, branding and strategic partnerships. She writes her own letter in the annual report.

people.name: Ashish Desai
people.bio: A chartered accountant with a B.Com from Gujarat University and over 25 years in accounting, budgeting, audit, costing and tax. Before Hester he was CFO of Blue Ray Aviation and, earlier, of Shreeyam Power & Steel Industries, a listed company with about ₹1,200 crore of revenue. He joined Hester as Group Finance Controller and was promoted to CFO in November 2025. He has worked on financial restructuring, trade finance, treasury and internal controls.
